definition_zh: 首要的；主要的；最好的；上等的；青春；壮年；全盛时期；使做好准备；注水启动
definition_en: most important or of the best quality; the strongest period of a person's life; to prepare something in advance so that it is ready to work
core_image: 一排名字里被红圈标在最前面的那一个
scene: 董事会名单上，排在最前面的那个名字被圈了出来，旁边还写着一行小字：此事由他拍板。 His prime task that morning was to count every crate in the store.
sceneCN: 这里 prime 是「首要的、最主要的」（第 1 个义项：最重要的）；句意为那天早上他的头等任务是清点店里的每一个木箱。图中可辨识物件：名单、红圈、批注小字。

pos.zh: 首要的；主要的；最好的；上等的
使做好准备；预先交代；（给泵）注水启动

collocations.zh: 给泵注水；投入资金启动经济
让学生为考试做好准备

derivatives.zh: 由 prime 加 -er 构成，早期指「第一本书」，今指入门读物
由拉丁词干 prim- 加 -acy 构成，义为「首位；首要地位」
由拉丁语 primus 加 -al 构成，义为「最初的；原始的」
由 primary 加 -ly 构成，义为「主要地；首先」

senses.title: Most important
senses.definition: more important than anything else in a particular situation
senses.definitionCN: 在某一情形中比其余一切都重要
senses.example: Safety is the prime concern when the old bridge is repaired.
senses.exampleCN: 修这座旧桥时，安全是最要紧的事。
senses.why: The root simply means first, and the first item on a list of concerns is the one that outranks all the others.
senses.whyCN: 词根只表示「第一」，而在需要操心的一串事情里排第一，就是压过其余所有项的那一件，于是「第一」自然读成「最要紧」。

senses.title: Of the best quality
senses.definition: of the highest quality or in the best condition, as of meat, land or a position
senses.definitionCN: 质量最高、状态最好的，如肉、土地或位置
senses.example: The market sells prime beef from farms nearby.
senses.exampleCN: 这个市场卖的是附近农场出产的优质牛肉。
senses.why: What ranks first is also the pick of the lot, so the ranking word comes to describe the best cut or the best spot.
senses.whyCN: 排在第一的东西往往也是同类里被挑出来的那一个，于是这个表示次序的词又用来形容最好的一块肉、最好的一个位置。

senses.title: The best years of life
senses.definition: the period of life when a person is strongest and most capable
senses.definitionCN: 一个人体力与能力最强的那段人生时期
senses.example: He was in the prime of life when he took over the farm.
senses.exampleCN: 他接手农场时正当壮年。
senses.why: A life also has a first and best stretch, so the word for what comes first was applied to the years before decline.
senses.whyCN: 人生也有最靠前、最好的那一段，于是表示「最先」的词被用来指衰退到来之前的那几年。

senses.title: To make ready in advance
senses.definition: to prepare a person, a machine or a pump beforehand so that it is ready to act
senses.definitionCN: 事先把人、机器或水泵准备妥当，使其随时可以运作
senses.example: The nurse primed the pump before the water could flow.
senses.exampleCN: 护士先给水泵注了水，水才流得出来。
senses.why: Priming a gun or a pump literally means filling it first, so the verb keeps the idea of putting something in before use.
senses.whyCN: 给枪装药、给泵注水，字面上都是「先填进去」，所以这个动词始终带着「使用之前先装好」的意思。

intro.en: Prime goes back to the Latin adjective for first, and each sense preserves that position in a queue: first in importance, best in quality, earliest in life, prepared beforehand.
intro.cn: prime 可追到拉丁语中表示「第一」的形容词，每个义项都保留着「排在最前」的位置感：最要紧、最好、人生最早的一段、事先备好。

items.en: A reconstructed root usually written as *per- meant forward or before, and it is generally thought to lie behind the Latin word for first.
items.cn: 一般认为，一个重构形式写作 *per- 的词根表示「向前、在前面」，是拉丁语「第一」一词的更早来源。

items.en: Primus was the everyday Latin adjective for the first in order, rank or time.
items.cn: primus 是拉丁语中表示次序、等级或时间上「第一」的常用形容词。

items.en: The phrase prima hora, the first hour of daylight, gave a noun prima for the first hour of prayer, later felt as the early morning.
items.cn: prima hora 意为白天的第一个时辰，由此得到名词 prima，指第一个祈祷时辰，后来也被理解为清晨。

items.en: Old French used prim and its feminine prime for first, fine or delicate, and English borrowed the adjective in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语用 prim 及其阴性形式 prime 表示「第一的、精致的、纤细的」，英语在十四世纪借入了这个形容词。

items.en: Modern English uses prime for what ranks first, for the best years of life, and for the act of making a machine ready in advance.
items.cn: 现代英语用 prime 指排第一的事物、人生最好的岁月，以及让机器事先就绪的动作。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin stem for first; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for what outranks the rest.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「第一」词干上的词；近义组收表示压过其余者的形容词。

entries.definition: First in order or importance; also the earlier stage of schooling.
entries.definitionCN: 次序或重要性上第一的；也指初等教育的。

entries.definition: A first book that introduces a subject to beginners.
entries.definitionCN: 向初学者介绍某学科的入门书。

entries.definition: Belonging to the earliest and simplest stage of something.
entries.definitionCN: 属于事物最早、最简单阶段的；原始的。

entries.definition: The position of being first or most important.
entries.definitionCN: 居于首位或最重要的地位。

entries.definition: Highest in rank or importance among a group.
entries.definitionCN: 在一群中等级或重要性最高的。

entries.definition: Largest or most important of several things.
entries.definitionCN: 若干事物中最大或最重要的。

entries.definition: Most advanced or most respected in a field.
entries.definitionCN: 在某领域最前列或最受敬重的。

entries.definition: Best possible under the given conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 在既定条件下最好的；最优的。

normalIntro.en: The word rests on the single Latin adjective for first, and its senses measure that position in lists, in quality, in a lifetime and in preparation.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词只依托拉丁语中「第一」这一个形容词，各义项分别把这一位置放到名单、品质、一生和准备工作里去衡量。

normal.en: Primus is Latin for first, so prime always carries a ranking: first in importance, first in quality, first years of life.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 primus 意为第一，所以 prime 始终带着排序：最要紧、最好、人生最初的那几年。

normal.en: A prime minister is the first minister, the one ranked above the rest of the cabinet.
normal.cn: prime minister 字面是「第一位大臣」，即排在其余内阁成员之前的那位。

normal.en: Prime time is the first-choice slot of the evening, when the largest audience is watching.
normal.cn: prime time 是晚间最被看重的时段，收看的人最多。

normal.en: To prime a pump is to pour water in first, before the pump can draw anything up.
normal.cn: 给泵注水，就是在泵能抽水之前先把水灌进去。

normal.en: Prince is built from the same primus plus capere, to take: a prince is the one who takes first place.
normal.cn: prince 也由同一个 primus 加 capere（取）构成，原意是「占取第一位的人」。

abstract.en: Picture a queue: prime is the person standing at the very front, and everyone else is measured from that spot.
abstract.cn: 想象一列队伍：prime 就是站在最前面的那个人，其余人都以这个位置为参照。

abstract.en: The same front position becomes the first hour of a day, the strongest years of a life, and the water poured in before a pump starts.
abstract.cn: 同一个「最前」的位置，可以变成一天里的第一个时辰、一生中最强的那几年，以及泵启动前先灌进去的水。

abstract.en: Anything primed has been filled in advance, so the word ties being early to being ready.
abstract.cn: 凡是 primed 的东西都是提前装好的，所以这个词把「早」和「就绪」绑在了一起。

examples.en: The prime cause of the fire was a faulty wire.
examples.cn: 这场火灾的首要起因是一根故障电线。

examples.en: She bought a piece of prime land near the river.
examples.cn: 她在河边买了一块上好的地。

examples.en: He is past his prime but still plays well.
examples.cn: 他已过了巅峰期，但球还打得不错。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普赖姆」——谐音像「扑来第一」，扑过去抢到最前面，所以 prime 是首要的、第一的。

root: 拉丁语 primus（第一、最前）经古法语进入英语；同族词多与「第一、最初」有关。prime 与 prince 都出自 primus，但 prince 的后半截来自 capere（取），原意是「占第一位的人」。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is first place; from that position the senses spread to the best quality, the strongest years of life, and the act of loading something in advance.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「排第一的位置」；义项由此分到最好的品质、人生最强的岁月，以及事先把东西装进去的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one name circled at the very top of a list.
core.cn: 核心意象：名单最上方被圈出的那一个名字。

branches.en: the first name on a list of worries
branches.cn: 一列操心之事里排第一的那个名字

branches.en: a captain putting the crew above the schedule
branches.cn: 船长把船员安全放在进度之前

branches.en: the best cut of beef on the butcher's block
branches.cn: 肉案上最好的一块牛肉

branches.en: a farmer in his strongest years taking over the land
branches.cn: 正当壮年的农夫接手田地

branches.en: water poured into a pump before it can draw
branches.cn: 水泵先注水才能抽水

intro.en: A Latin adjective for first, plus a handful of English endings that turn it into a noun, an adverb and a beginner's book.
intro.cn: 一个表示「第一」的拉丁形容词，再加几个英语词尾，就变出了名词、副词和入门书。

latinIntro.en: Latin primus, first, also produced primarius, of the first rank, and the family reached English through Old French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 primus（第一）还派生出 primarius（第一等的），这一族词经古法语进入英语。

items.meaningCN: 次序或重要性上第一的

definition_en: great honour and praise, or magnificent beauty
core_image: 夕阳把整座山谷染成金色，人群静静仰望
scene: 他们为荣誉而战。 They fought for glory.
sceneCN: 这里 glory 是「荣誉」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他们为荣誉而战。

derivatives.zh: 光荣的；壮丽的

senses.title: Honour and praise
senses.definition: great honour won by achievement
senses.definitionCN: 因成就而赢得的巨大荣誉
senses.example: They fought for glory.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为荣誉而战。
senses.why: This is the central sense of public honour.
senses.whyCN: 这是表示公众荣誉的核心含义。

senses.title: Magnificent beauty
senses.definition: impressive beauty and splendour
senses.definitionCN: 令人赞叹的美与辉煌
senses.example: The glory of the sunset filled the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 落日的壮丽充满了山谷。
senses.why: Glory was also a radiance, so it names visible splendour.
senses.whyCN: glory 也曾指光辉，因此也命名可见的壮丽。

senses.title: Praise in worship
senses.definition: praise given to God in religious language
senses.definitionCN: 宗教语言中献给上帝的赞美
senses.example: Glory to God in the highest.
senses.exampleCN: 在至高之处荣耀归于上帝。
senses.why: The religious sense is the oldest use of the word.
senses.whyCN: 宗教义是这个词最古老的用法。

intro.en: Glory came from Latin through French into English.
intro.cn: glory 从拉丁语经法语进入英语。

items.en: Gloria meant glory, fame, and praise.
items.cn: gloria 意为荣耀、名声与赞美。

items.en: Glorie carried the word into French.
items.cn: glorie 把这个词带入法语。

items.en: Glory named honour and religious praise.
items.cn: glory 指荣誉与宗教赞美。

items.en: It also named the beauty of light and landscape.
items.cn: 它也指光线与景色的壮美。

items.en: Glory days fixed the word in memories of success.
items.cn: glory days 把这个词固定在成功的回忆中。

note.en: Glory is compared with look-alike words and words for honour.
note.cn: 把 glory 与形近词以及表示荣誉的词作比较。

the earth

respect and high regard
the state of being well known

normalIntro.en: Glory is honour that shines and is seen.
normalIntro.cn: glory 是会发光、被看见的荣誉。

normal.en: They fought for glory.
normal.cn: 他们为荣誉而战。

normal.en: The glory of the sunset filled the valley.
normal.cn: 落日的壮丽充满了山谷。

normal.en: Glory to God in the highest.
normal.cn: 在至高之处荣耀归于上帝。

normal.en: The team recalled its glory days.
normal.cn: 这支队伍回想起昔日的辉煌。

normal.en: Her hair was her crowning glory.
normal.cn: 她的头发是她最光彩的部分。

abstract.en: Glory is the shadow success casts on other people.
abstract.cn: 荣耀，是成功投在他人身上的影子。

abstract.en: What is done for glory alone fades with the crowd.
abstract.cn: 只为荣耀而做的事，会随人群散去。

abstract.en: True glory is quiet in the one who has it.
abstract.cn: 真正的荣誉，在拥有它的人身上是安静的。

dict_mnemonic.text: glory 加 -ous 成 glorious（光荣的），加 -fy 成 glorify（颂扬）；glory days 是「辉煌岁月」，in glory 是「在荣耀中」，注意与 glove（手套）区分。

root: 来自拉丁语 gloria（荣耀、名声），经古法语 glorie 进入英语，核心义由「宗教赞美」扩展到「荣誉」与「壮丽」。

sensesIntro.en: Glory means honour won by achievement, visible splendour, or praise in worship.
sensesIntro.cn: glory 指因成就赢得的荣誉、可见的壮丽，或宗教中的赞美。

core.en: Praise and light gathered around a person or thing.
core.cn: 聚集在人事物周围的光与赞美。

branches.en: A winner lifts a cup before a crowd.
branches.cn: 获胜者在人群前举起奖杯。

branches.en: A valley turns gold at sunset.
branches.cn: 山谷在日落时变成金色。

branches.en: Voices rise together in a church.
branches.cn: 教堂里众人齐声歌唱。

branches.en: Honour and radiance are two faces of one light.
branches.cn: 荣誉与光辉，是同一道光的两面。

branches.en: Heavenly praise borrows the language of light.
branches.cn: 天上的赞美，借用了光的语言。

intro.en: Glory forms adjectives, verbs, and nouns with -ous, -fy, and -ation.
intro.cn: glory 与 -ous、-fy、-ation 构成形容词、动词和名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is gloria, praise and fame.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁词根是 gloria，意为赞美与名声。

items.example: The book tells the glories of the past.
items.exampleCN: 这本书讲述昔日的荣耀。
他们赢得了一场光荣的胜利。

items.example: It is just a glorified shed.
items.exampleCN: 那不过是个被美化了的棚子。

items.example: The film is a glorification of youth.
items.exampleCN: 这部电影是对青春的颂扬。
那是一场不光彩的失败。

definition_zh: 向下地；往下；往下层；由高到低
definition_en: toward a lower place, level, or rank; the adverb form of downward
core_image: 水流顺着台阶一级一级往下淌
scene: 雨水沿着屋檐汇成细流，顺着石阶一直往下。 The water ran downwards along the stone steps.
sceneCN: 这里 downwards 是「向下地」（第 1 个义项）；句意是水沿着石阶向下流。

pos.zh: 副词：向下地；往下；由高到低

derivatives.zh: 去掉副词词尾 -s 的形式，义为「向下的」，也可作副词
由 up 加 -ward 再加副词词尾 -s 构成，义为「向上地」，与 downwards 方向相反

senses.title: Toward a lower place
senses.definition: in a direction from a higher position to a lower one
senses.definitionCN: 沿从较高位置到较低位置的方向
senses.example: He glanced downwards at the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 他朝下望向山谷。
senses.why: The -s ending marks the adverb, so downwards describes the manner of a movement rather than naming a thing.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -s 标示副词，所以 downwards 描述动作的方式，而不是给某个东西命名。

senses.title: Toward a lower amount or rank
senses.definition: toward a smaller number, a lower level, or a lower position in a scale
senses.definitionCN: 朝更小的数字、更低的水平或更低的等级去
senses.example: The forecast was revised downwards by two points.
senses.exampleCN: 预测被向下修正了两个点。
senses.why: Once the direction word covers numbers, the adverb can describe any adjustment toward a lower figure.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个方向词覆盖了数字，副词就能描述任何朝更低的数值所作的调整。

senses.title: From the top through all lower levels
senses.definition: starting at the highest level and continuing through every level below
senses.definitionCN: 从最高层开始，一直贯穿其下每一层
senses.example: The order was passed downwards through every department.
senses.exampleCN: 命令自上而下一级级传达到每个部门。
senses.why: A direction that keeps going down becomes a way of describing the whole order of levels, not one single step.
senses.whyCN: 当方向一直往下延伸，它就不再是单步动作，而变成描述整个层级顺序的方式。

intro.en: Downwards is downward plus an adverbial -s that became common in the Middle English period.
intro.cn: downwards 是 downward 加上一个副词性的 -s，这种写法在中古英语时期流行起来。

items.en: Dun meant hill, and its dative dune gave the direction word down.
items.cn: 古英语 dun 意为「山丘」，其与格 dune 给出方向词 down。

items.en: The suffix weard meant turned toward and produced directional words.
items.cn: 后缀 weard 意为「朝向」，构成一批方向词。

items.en: Writers began adding -s to adverbs such as downwards and afterwards, perhaps by analogy with genitive forms.
items.cn: 作家开始给 downwards、afterwards 这类副词加 -s，可能是类比属格形式而来。

items.en: Downwards was established in print, though the earliest attestations are not precisely dated.
items.cn: downwards 在印刷文本中确立，不过最早用例的精确年代不确定。

items.en: British English keeps the -s adverb, while American English usually prefers downward for both uses.
items.cn: 英式英语保留带 -s 的副词，美式英语则两种词性多用 downward。

note.en: The look-alike group differs only in the ending; the near-meaning group offers other downward adverbs.
note.cn: 形近组只在词尾上有差别；近义组提供其他表示「向下」的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective form, also used as an adverb in American English.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词形式，在美式英语中也作副词，是 downwards 的基础形式。

entries.definition: At a later time; it shares the adverbial -s.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「后来」，共享同一个副词词尾 -s。

entries.definition: In the direction of; another British -s adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「朝、向」，同样带英式副词词尾 -s。

entries.definition: At or to a lower position, without implying motion.
entries.definitionCN: 副词或介词，义为「在下面」，不含移动过程。

entries.definition: In or to a lower position; also a comparative adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 副词或形容词，义为「更低」，兼作比较级。

entries.definition: With the head first and great speed, often recklessly.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「头朝下地、莽撞地」，带有失控的意味。

normalIntro.en: These hooks separate the -s adverb from the plain adjective and keep the level image.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把带 -s 的副词与朴素形容词分开，并保住「层级」的画面。

normal.en: The -s marks an adverb, just as in afterwards and towards.
normal.cn: 这个 -s 是副词标记，afterwards 与 towards 同理。

normal.en: Downward can do both jobs in America, but British usage splits them.
normal.cn: 美式英语里 downward 两职兼挑，英式则把两者分开。

normal.en: Revised downwards means the number was pushed toward the floor.
normal.cn: revised downwards 就是数字被朝地面方向压下去。

normal.en: From the top downwards runs through every level, not just one step.
normal.cn: from the top downwards 贯穿每一层，而不只是一步。

normal.en: The word never names a place; it always describes how something moves.
normal.cn: 这个词从不指某个地方，它只描述事物如何移动。

abstract.en: Picture rain threading down a stone staircase.
abstract.cn: 想象雨水沿着石阶一级级往下淌。

abstract.en: Picture a lift panel where every arrow points at the floor.

sensesIntro.en: The adverb covers three downward movements: through space, through numbers, and through a whole ladder of levels.

definition_zh: 减去；负的；零下的；减号；缺点
definition_en: with the subtraction of; lower than zero; and, as a noun, the negative sign or a disadvantage counted against something
core_image: 算式里一道短横，把一堆东西划掉一部分
scene: 冬夜的站牌下，温度计的红线缩到最低一格，广播里报出冷得刺骨的读数。 The overnight reading fell to minus eleven degrees.
sceneCN: 这里是「零下的、负的」（第 2 个义项：低于零的读数）；句意为夜里的读数降到了零下十一度。图中可辨识物件：温度计、站牌、结霜的玻璃。

pos.zh: 减号；负号；缺点；不利因素

derivatives.zh: 与 minus 同出拉丁语比较级 minor（更小的），义为「较小的；次要的」
由拉丁语 minimus（最小）而来，与 minus 同族，义为「最小值；最低限度」
由 minimum 词干加 -ize 构成，义为「使减到最少；轻视」
源自拉丁语 minusculus（略小的），与 minus 共用「小」这一词根，义为「极小的」

senses.title: Taking one amount away from another
senses.definition: used between two numbers or amounts to show that the second is taken away from the first
senses.definitionCN: 用在两个数或数量之间，表示把后一个从前一个里拿掉
senses.example: Ten minus four leaves six.
senses.exampleCN: 十减四余六。
senses.why: Latin minus is the neuter of minor, the comparative of parvus, and it meant less; arithmetic simply took that comparative word and put it between two amounts.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 minus 是 minor 的中性形式，而 minor 是 parvus 的比较级，本义是「更少」；算术只是把这个比较级词放到两个数量之间。

senses.title: Below zero on a scale
senses.definition: lower than zero, especially of a temperature or a value on a numbered scale
senses.definitionCN: 低于零，尤指温度或某个有刻度的数值
senses.example: The overnight reading fell to minus eleven degrees.
senses.exampleCN: 夜里的读数降到了零下十一度。
senses.why: If minus marks what is less, a value carrying the word is literally less than nothing; the same marker is reused to name readings on the far side of zero.
senses.whyCN: 既然 minus 标的是「更少」，带上它的数值就字面上「比没有还少」；于是同一个标记又被用来称呼零另一侧的那些读数。

senses.title: The written sign of subtraction
senses.definition: the short horizontal sign that shows a number is being subtracted or is negative
senses.definitionCN: 表示做减法或数值为负的那道短横
senses.example: Write a minus before the figure to show a loss.
senses.exampleCN: 在数字前写一个减号来表示亏损。
senses.why: A mark that performs an operation ends up being called by the operation's own name, the way the plus names its cross, so the stroke itself became a minus.
senses.whyCN: 执行某个运算的记号，最后被运算本身的名字来称呼，正如加号叫 plus 一样，这道横也被叫作 minus。

senses.title: A disadvantage counted against something
senses.definition: a feature that makes a person or thing less good, usually weighed against a plus
senses.definitionCN: 使人或事物显得差一些的特点，通常与某个优点相权衡
senses.example: The only minus of the flat is its distance from the station.
senses.exampleCN: 这套房子唯一的缺点是离车站太远。
senses.why: In an account, losses are written in the column of subtracted numbers; speakers moved that mark into everyday judgement, so any loss of quality is now called a minus.
senses.whyCN: 在账本里，亏损写在被减去的数字那一栏；说话人把这个标记搬进日常评价，于是任何品质上的失分都被叫作 minus。

intro.en: Minus is Latin for less, the neuter of a comparative adjective meaning smaller, and it reached English through written arithmetic before spreading to signs and to judgements.
intro.cn: minus 是拉丁语中表示「更少」的词，是意为「更小」的比较级的中性形式；它先随笔算进入英语，再扩散到符号与评价用语。

items.en: Minus was the neuter of minor, the comparative of parvus, and it meant less or smaller in comparisons of quantity.
items.cn: minus 是 minor 的中性形式，而 minor 是 parvus 的比较级，在比较数量时表示「更少、更小」。

items.en: Later Latin calculation used minus in phrases where one number was taken from another, fixing the word inside the language of reckoning.
items.cn: 后来的拉丁语计算在「从一个数里取走另一个数」的说法里用 minus，把这个词固定进了算账的语言。

items.en: English adopted minus, together with plus, when written arithmetic spread through trade and schooling in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 十六世纪，随着笔算通过贸易与学校教育传开，英语把 minus 与 plus 一并借入。

items.en: The noun minus appeared for the sign itself and for a negative quantity, so operation, mark and value came to share one form.
items.cn: 名词 minus 出现，用来指符号本身和负的数量，于是运算、记号与数值共用同一个词形。

items.en: Modern English counts minuses in ordinary judgement, so a drawback is entered like a loss on an imaginary balance sheet.
items.cn: 现代英语还在日常评价里数 minus，把缺点像亏损一样记在一张想象中的账本上。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin comparative behind minus and its family of smallness; the near-meaning group gathers words for taking away and for below-zero values.
note.cn: 形近组顺着 minus 背后的拉丁比较级与「小」的词族展开；近义组收表示取走与零下数值的词。

normalIntro.en: The word began as a comparative meaning less, and its family keeps shrinking: smaller, least, to lessen, and finally a mark that records the loss.

normal.en: Minus is the neuter of the Latin comparative minor, so the idea of smaller sits inside the word before subtraction ever appears.
normal.cn: minus 是拉丁比较级 minor 的中性形式，所以在「减法」出现之前，这个词里已经装着「更小」。

normal.en: Plus and minus were borrowed as a pair, which is why the two signs are learned together on the same page of arithmetic.
normal.cn: plus 与 minus 是成对借入的，所以两个符号总是在算术的同一页上一起学。

normal.en: The noun came after the preposition: first the act of taking away, then the stroke that stands for the act.
normal.cn: 名词出现在介词之后：先是「取走」这个动作，然后才是代表这个动作的那道横。

normal.en: Minimum, minimize and minimal all descend from the same Latin family, so the sense of least runs through every one of them.
normal.cn: minimum、minimize 与 minimal 都出自同一拉丁词族，所以「最少」的意思贯穿它们每一个。

normal.en: A minus in a judgement borrows the ledger: losses are written in the same column as subtracted numbers.
normal.cn: 评价里的 minus 借用了账本：亏损与被减去的数字写在同一栏。

abstract.en: Picture a full pan on a scale, then a hand lifting part of the load away.
abstract.cn: 想象天平上满满一盘，然后一只手把其中一部分搬走。

abstract.en: A word for less becomes a stroke on paper, then a fault in a report: smallness travels from quantity to value.
abstract.cn: 一个表示「更少」的词变成纸上的一道横，再变成报告里的一个毛病：小从数量走到了价值。

abstract.en: Every minus presupposes something to subtract from; a loss only makes sense against a starting amount.
abstract.cn: 每个 minus 都以「有东西可减」为前提；亏损只有对着起始的数量才有意义。

examples.en: Ten minus four leaves six.
examples.cn: 十减四余六。

examples.en: The temperature fell to minus nine overnight.
examples.cn: 夜里温度降到了零下九度。

examples.en: The only minus of the plan is its cost.
examples.cn: 这个计划唯一的缺点是成本太高。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「麦纳斯」——一袋麦子被拿走了，剩下的就少了；记住 minus 是减去，也指减号与缺点。

root: 拉丁语 minus（更少）是 minor（更小）的中性形式，源头为 parvus（小）；先用于算术的减法，再指负值与减号，后引申为缺点。

sensesIntro.en: The core is taking an amount away; the senses then reach the readings below zero, the mark that performs the taking, and the drawbacks people weigh like losses.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「取走一部分」；义项由此走到零下的读数、执行取走的那道记号，以及人们在评价中像亏损一样权衡的缺点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a short horizontal stroke cancelling part of a row of marks.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道短横划掉一排记号中的一部分。

branches.en: a hand lifting part of the load off a scale
branches.cn: 一只手把天平上的东西搬走一部分

branches.en: a thermometer sinking past the zero mark
branches.cn: 温度计的水银沉到零刻度以下

branches.en: a stroke written in front of a figure
branches.cn: 数字前面写下的那道横

branches.en: a short list of pros with one item on the wrong side
branches.cn: 优点清单里有一条落到了反方

branches.en: the same mark serving a reading and a written sign
branches.cn: 同一个记号，一次服务读数，一次服务书写

intro.en: A Latin comparative supplies the stem, and its family of smallness plus two English affixes carry the word into arithmetic and into everyday judgement.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁比较级提供词干，它的「小」词族再加上两个英语词缀，把这个词带进算术与日常评价。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: to make, to cause to be

definition_zh: 龙；凶恶的人；蜥蜴类；严厉的女监护人
definition_en: a large mythical beast that breathes fire, or a fierce and frightening person
core_image: 鳞片覆身、张口喷火的巨兽伏在山口
scene: 古庙门前雕着一条盘绕的长兽，鳞片在香火里泛红。 The carved dragon guards the temple gate.
sceneCN: 这里 dragon 是「龙」（第 1 个义项）；句意是那条雕刻的龙守着庙门。

pos.zh: 名词：龙；凶恶的人；蜥蜴类

derivatives.zh: 由 dragon 加 fly 复合而成，义为「蜻蜓」
由 dragon 加 -ish 构成，义为「像龙的；凶猛的」

senses.title: A fire-breathing mythical beast
senses.definition: a large imaginary animal in stories, often with wings, claws and fiery breath
senses.definitionCN: 传说中大型的想象动物，常有翅膀、利爪与喷火的能力
senses.example: The story ends with the knight killing a dragon.
senses.exampleCN: 故事以骑士杀死一条龙告终。
senses.why: Greek drakon first named a huge staring serpent, and that staring, gleaming creature is the ancestor of the modern dragon.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 drakon 最初指一条巨大、目光炯炯的蛇，正是那种瞪视、鳞光闪闪的形象成了今天「龙」的祖先。

senses.title: A fierce or cruel person
senses.definition: a person who is very fierce, strict, or frightening
senses.definitionCN: 非常凶悍、严厉或令人害怕的人
senses.example: Our new manager is a real dragon about deadlines.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的新经理在截止日期上凶得厉害。
senses.why: Because the beast is fearsome, calling a person a dragon transfers the same menace onto them.
senses.whyCN: 因为这种兽令人生畏，把人称作 dragon，就是把同样的凶气转移到那个人身上。

senses.title: A small tropical lizard
senses.definition: a small lizard of warm regions, often with a fold of skin at the throat
senses.definitionCN: 产于温暖地区的小型蜥蜴，喉部常有皮褶
senses.example: A green dragon basked on the warm rock.
senses.exampleCN: 一只绿色的蜥蜴在温热的岩石上晒太阳。
senses.why: Small scaly reptiles look like miniature versions of the mythical beast, so biologists reused the name.
senses.whyCN: 披鳞的小爬行动物像是传说巨兽的缩小版，于是生物学家复用了这个名字。

senses.title: The Chinese imperial emblem
senses.definition: the long serpentine creature of Chinese art, a symbol of power and good fortune
senses.definitionCN: 中国艺术中修长的蛇形神兽，象征权力与吉祥
senses.example: The dragon on the robe marked the emperor alone.
senses.exampleCN: 袍上的龙纹只属于皇帝。
senses.why: When the Western word met Chinese art, the same name was given to a very different, auspicious creature.
senses.whyCN: 当西方的这个词遇到中国艺术，同一个名称被安到了一种截然不同、象征祥瑞的动物身上。

intro.en: Dragon came through Latin and French from Greek drakon, a huge serpent, and the word has always implied a stare.
intro.cn: dragon 经拉丁语与法语来自希腊语 drakon，意为巨蛇，这个词从一开始就含「瞪视」的意味。

items.en: Drakon meant a large serpent, and it is usually linked to a verb meaning to look sharply or flash.
items.cn: drakon 意为巨蛇，一般认为它与表示「锐利地看、闪动」的动词有关。

items.en: Latin borrowed the word as draco and used it for serpents and for a military standard.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入作 draco，用来指蛇类，也指一种军旗。

items.en: Old French passed the word into the shape that English borrowed.
items.cn: 古法语把这个词传成英语借入时的形态。

items.en: English dragon first appears in religious and monster stories; the exact earliest text is debated.
items.cn: 英语 dragon 最早出现在宗教与怪物故事里；最早的文本究竟是哪一篇仍有争议。

items.en: The name spread to fierce people, to small lizards, and to the auspicious beast of Chinese art.
items.cn: 这个名字扩散到凶悍的人、小型蜥蜴，以及中国艺术中象征祥瑞的神兽。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on dragon or its Greek source; the near-meaning group gathers mythical creatures.
note.cn: 形近组建在 dragon 或其希腊语源头之上；近义组收的是其他神话生物。

entries.definition: The Latin form of the word, used for serpents and a constellation.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语形式，指蛇类，也是天龙座的名称。

entries.definition: A long-bodied flying insect with large transparent wings.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「蜻蜓」，由 dragon 与 fly 复合而成。

entries.definition: Resembling a dragon; fierce.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「像龙的；凶猛的」，由 dragon 加 -ish 构成。

entries.definition: A large snake, often in myths and older stories.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「巨蛇」，是 dragon 在希腊语时期的近邻概念。

entries.definition: A large or dangerous animal, real or imagined.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「野兽」，可指真实或想象的凶猛动物。

entries.definition: A mythical creature with wings and two legs, distinct from a four-legged dragon.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「双足飞龙」，是龙类传说中的一个分支，与四足龙有别。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the Greek staring serpent and the modern reuse of the name.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子沿着希腊语「瞪视的巨蛇」，以及这个名称的现代复用展开。

normal.en: Drakon meant a serpent that stares, and its glare survives in the modern beast.
normal.cn: drakon 指瞪视的巨蛇，那股瞪人的气势一直留在今天的龙形象里。

normal.en: Dragonfly keeps the beast's name on a harmless insect.
normal.cn: dragonfly 把这头巨兽的名字安在一种无害的昆虫上。

normal.en: Calling a strict manager a dragon borrows the beast's temper.
normal.cn: 把严厉的经理称作 dragon，是借用了这头兽的脾气。

normal.en: The Chinese dragon is a long serpent of good fortune, not a fire-breather.
normal.cn: 中国的龙是象征吉祥的长蛇形神兽，而不是喷火的怪兽。

normal.en: The dragon boat race keeps the name in celebration rather than fear.
normal.cn: 龙舟赛让这个名字从恐惧转向庆典。

abstract.en: Picture a carved beast coiled around a temple gate.
abstract.cn: 想象一头雕刻的巨兽盘绕在庙门旁。

abstract.en: Picture a shining eye opening in the dark.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗中一只发亮的眼睛睁开。

abstract.en: Picture a lizard on a hot stone suddenly looking huge.
abstract.cn: 想象石上晒太阳的蜥蜴忽然看起来变得巨大。

examples.en: In the tale, the dragon guards a cave of gold.
examples.cn: 故事里，那条龙守着一洞黄金。

examples.en: She can be a dragon when the rules are broken.
examples.cn: 一旦有人违规，她就会变得很凶。

examples.en: Dragon boat races fill the river every summer.
examples.cn: 每年夏天，龙舟赛让整条河热闹起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「抓根」——传说中龙用爪子抓地，重新扎根，一看到就想起这条巨兽。

root: 经拉丁语 draco 与古法语来自希腊语 drakon（巨蛇）。drakon 一般认为与表示「锐利地看、闪动」的词有关，因为巨蛇的形象核心是瞪视与鳞光。英语借入后既指传说巨兽，也引申指凶悍的人、小型蜥蜴，并被挪用于中国艺术中的祥瑞神兽。

sensesIntro.en: One staring serpent in myth becomes a monster, a fierce person, a small lizard and an auspicious emblem.
sensesIntro.cn: 神话里一条瞪视的巨蛇，变成了怪兽、凶人、小蜥蜴与祥瑞纹样。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scaled beast coiled at a gate with burning eyes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一头鳞甲巨兽盘在门边，眼睛发亮。

branches.en: MONSTER: the first sense is the mythical beast of story and art.
branches.cn: 怪兽线：第一个义项是故事与艺术中的传说巨兽。

branches.en: PERSON: the beast's temper transfers to a fierce human being.
branches.cn: 人物线：巨兽的脾气被转移到凶悍的人身上，即第二个义项。

branches.en: LIZARD: small scaly reptiles borrow the ancient name.
branches.cn: 爬行线：披鳞的小爬行动物借用了这个古老名称，即第三个义项。

branches.en: CHINESE ART: the name was reused for a long, auspicious serpent.
branches.cn: 东方线：这个名字又被挪用于修长、象征祥瑞的神兽，即第四个义项。

branches.en: The monster and the fierce person share exactly the same menace.
branches.cn: 怪兽与凶人，共享同一种令人畏惧的气场。

intro.en: Dragon is a whole borrowed word, but English freely builds compounds and derived forms on it.
intro.cn: dragon 是整体借来的词，但英语仍能自由地用它造复合词与派生词。

latinIntro.en: Latin draco is recorded, and Greek drakon stands behind it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 draco 有文献记录，其背后是希腊语 drakon。

items.example: The Greek noun is the earliest source.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊名词是最早的来源。

items.example: Latin carried the word to Europe.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语把这个词带到欧洲。

derivatives.zh: 由 dragon 加 fly 复合，义为「蜻蜓」
由 dragon 加 -ish 构成，义为「像龙的」

definition_en: a substance used to give colour to cloth, hair or other materials, to colour something with it, or to give a deep lasting colour
core_image: 一块白布浸进深蓝色的染缸，提起来时颜色已经吃进纤维
scene: 作坊里一口大染缸冒着热气，白布被慢慢浸下去。 The cloth was soaked in a blue dye.
sceneCN: 这里 dye 是「染料」（第 1 个义项：给织物上色的物质）；句意是那块布被浸在蓝色染料里。

pos.zh: 动词：给……染色；使染上颜色

derivatives.zh: 由本词加施事后缀 -er 构成，义为「染工；染色者」
由本词与 stuff 复合，义为「染料；着色剂」
由 dyed 与 in the wool 组成的习语，义为「彻头彻尾的；顽固的」

senses.title: A colouring substance
senses.definition: a natural or chemical substance used to give colour to cloth, hair or other materials
senses.definitionCN: 用来给布料、头发或其他材料上色的天然或化学物质
senses.example: The cloth was soaked in a blue dye.
senses.exampleCN: 那块布被浸在蓝色染料里。
senses.why: This is the concrete core: a substance whose only job is to transfer colour into a material.
senses.whyCN: 这是具体的核心：一种唯一任务就是把颜色送进材料里的物质。

senses.title: To colour with a dye
senses.definition: to give something a colour by putting it into a dye or applying dye to it
senses.definitionCN: 把某物放进染液或把染料涂上去，使其带有颜色
senses.example: She dyed her coat dark green.
senses.exampleCN: 她把外套染成了深绿色。
senses.why: The verb is the noun in action: the substance enters the material and changes its colour.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是名词在动作中：物质进入材料，改变了它的颜色。

senses.title: To colour deeply or lastingly
senses.definition: to give something a strong or lasting colour, often used of light or of a figurative change
senses.definitionCN: 给某物强烈的或持久的颜色，常用于光线或比喻性的变化
senses.example: The sunset dyed the sky orange.
senses.exampleCN: 落日把天空染成了橙色。
senses.why: Once a dye is fixed, the colour will not wash out, so the verb extends to any deep and lasting tint.
senses.whyCN: 染料一旦固定，颜色就洗不掉，于是这个动词扩展到任何浓重而持久的着色。

intro.en: Dye is a native Old English word for colour and for the act of colouring, later narrowed to the substance and its use.
intro.cn: dye 是本族语古英语词，原指颜色与上色的动作，后来收窄为染料及其使用。

items.en: A Germanic noun and verb for colouring are reconstructed, though the exact forms and their deeper origin are uncertain.
items.cn: 日耳曼语中被重构出表示「上色」的名词与动词，但其确切形式与更早来源不确定。

items.en: Old English had a noun for colour or dye and a verb meaning to colour, both from the same family.
items.cn: 古英语有表示「颜色、染料」的名词，也有表示「上色」的动词，二者同属一族。

items.en: Middle English kept the noun for the substance and the verb for the action, and the spelling moved toward dye.
items.cn: 中古英语保留了表示物质的名词和表示动作的动词，拼写逐渐走向 dye。

items.en: Dyeing became a major trade, and dye, dyer and dyestuff fixed the workshop vocabulary.
items.cn: 染色在十六世纪成为重要行业，dye、dyer、dyestuff 固定了作坊里的词汇。

items.en: The figurative sense of colouring light or a mood appears alongside the industrial sense.
items.cn: 给光线或情绪「染色」的比喻义与工业义同时存在。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on dye and one dangerous near-spelling; the near-meaning group separates colouring verbs by strength and method.
note.cn: 形近组收由 dye 构成的词形和一个易混拼写；近义组按强度与方法区分几个着色动词。

entries.definition: A person whose trade is dyeing cloth; dye plus -er.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「染工」，由 dye 加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: Any substance used as a dye; dye plus stuff.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「染料、着色剂」，由 dye 加 stuff 构成。

entries.definition: The process of colouring cloth; spelled with e to distinguish it from dying.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「染色工艺」，保留 e 是为了与 dying 区分。

entries.definition: The present participle of die; it sounds the same as dyeing but has no colour in it.
entries.definitionCN: die 的现在分词，与 dyeing 同音，却与颜色无关。

entries.definition: To give colour to something; the general verb, usable for paint, dye or light.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「给……上色」，通用词，可指颜料、染料或光。

entries.definition: To leave a mark or colour that is hard to remove, often accidentally.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「弄脏、染上痕迹」，常指意外留下难去的颜色。

entries.definition: To give a slight colour to something; softer and lighter than dye.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「给……淡淡上色」，比 dye 更轻更浅。

entries.definition: A dry colouring matter used in paint; a material rather than the action.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「颜料」，是涂料中的干性着色物质，指材料而非动作。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the colour from the vat into the fibre and then into the sky at sunset.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子跟着颜色从染缸进入纤维，再进入落日的天空。

normal.en: Dye is the substance; to dye is to put that substance into a material.
normal.cn: dye 是物质，to dye 是把这种物质送进材料。

normal.en: A dyer works with dye, and a dyestuff is any material that dyes.
normal.cn: dyer 与 dye 打交道，dyestuff 是任何能染色的材料。

normal.en: Dyeing keeps the e; dying from die does not, so the spelling marks the difference.
normal.cn: dyeing 保留 e，来自 die 的 dying 不留，拼写标出了区别。

normal.en: A blue dye in a vat can turn a whole bolt of cloth blue.
normal.cn: 染缸里的一缸蓝色染料能把整匹布染蓝。

normal.en: Sunset dyeing the sky is the same image, with light as the dye.
normal.cn: 落日染天空是同一个意象，只是光成了染料。

abstract.en: Picture white cloth disappearing into dark blue liquid and coming out changed.
abstract.cn: 想象白布没入深蓝的液体，再出来时已经变了颜色。

abstract.en: The same liquid, thinner, could be a tint; the same mark, accidental, could be a stain.
abstract.cn: 同样的液体淡一些就是 tint；同样的痕迹若是意外留下，就是 stain。

abstract.en: Dye is colour deciding to stay rather than sit on the surface.
abstract.cn: dye 是颜色决定留下来，而不是停在表面。

examples.en: The cloth was soaked in a blue dye.
examples.cn: 那块布被浸在蓝色染料里。

examples.en: She dyed her coat dark green.
examples.cn: 她把外套染成了深绿色。

examples.en: The sunset dyed the sky orange.
examples.cn: 落日把天空染成了橙色。

dict_mnemonic.text: dye 是一缸颜色：把布浸进去，颜色就吃进纤维，再也洗不掉。

root: 本族语古英语词，原有表示「颜色、染料」的名词与表示「上色」的动词，中古英语拼写逐渐固定为 dye。十六世纪染色业兴盛，dyer、dyestuff 等词进入作坊词汇。更早的日耳曼语形式与印欧语来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of dye move from the substance, to the act of applying it, to any deep and lasting colouring.
sensesIntro.cn: dye 的三个义项从染料这一物质，移到施加它的动作，再到任何浓重而持久的着色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: white cloth sinking into a vat of dark blue liquid.
core.cn: 核心意象：白布沉入一缸深蓝的染液。

branches.en: THE SUBSTANCE: the material whose purpose is to carry colour.
branches.cn: 物质线：以携带颜色为目的的材料。

branches.en: THE BATH: the cloth enters the liquid and comes out changed.
branches.cn: 染缸线：布进入液体，出来时已经变了颜色。

branches.en: THE LASTING TINT: colour that stays, even when the dye is light.
branches.cn: 持久着色线：颜色留了下来，即使染的是光。

branches.en: MATTER AND ACTION: the substance and the act share one name in English.
branches.cn: 物质与动作：物质和动作在英语里共用一个词。

branches.en: FROM CLOTH TO SKY: the same verb colours fabric and evening light.
branches.cn: 从布到天空：同一个动词既染织物，也染暮色。

intro.en: Dye is a native word; English builds dyer, dyestuff and dyeing with ordinary suffixes.
intro.cn: dye 是本族语词；英语用普通后缀构成 dyer、dyestuff 与 dyeing。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor; Latin tingere, to dye, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语祖先；拉丁语 tingere（染色）只是语义上的对应。

items.example: The word serves as noun and verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个词兼作名词与动词。

items.meaning: more than one; he or she does

derivatives.zh: 由本词加施事后缀 -er 构成，义为「染工；染色者」
由本词与 stuff 复合，义为「染料；着色剂」
由 dyed 与 in the wool 组成的习语，义为「彻头彻尾的；顽固的」

definition_zh: 无用的；无效的；差劲的；无能为力的
definition_en: not able to serve any purpose, with no effect, or of very poor quality
core_image: 雨伞的伞骨全断了，撑开只剩一块破布
scene: 雨下得正急，他打开那把旧伞，伞骨立刻折断，雨水顺着脖子流下来。 The broken umbrella was completely useless in that storm.
sceneCN: 这里 useless 是「无用的、不顶事的」（第 1 个义项：起不到应有的作用）；句意为那把坏伞在那场暴雨中完全没用。伞骨尽断的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 加 -ness 构成名词，义为「无用」
加 -ly 构成副词，义为「无用地」
换成肯定后缀 -ful，义为「有用的」
去掉后缀后的基础词，义为「使用」

senses.title: Unable to serve any purpose
senses.definition: not able to do what it is meant to do
senses.definitionCN: 做不到它本该做到的事情
senses.example: The old phone is useless because the screen will not turn on.
senses.exampleCN: 那部旧手机没用了，屏幕根本开不亮。
senses.why: The suffix -less means without, so the word simply says that no use can be found in the thing at all.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -less 意为「没有」，所以说得很直白：这东西里根本找不出用处。

senses.title: Having no effect on a result
senses.definition: producing no effect on the situation, however much effort is made
senses.definitionCN: 无论费多少力气，对局面都不产生任何影响
senses.example: Shouting at the referee was useless.
senses.exampleCN: 冲着裁判大喊毫无作用。
senses.why: If a tool cannot change anything, it is as good as broken; the same judgement passes to efforts and protests.
senses.whyCN: 工具改变不了任何事，就跟坏了一样；同样的判断于是也用在了努力与抗议上。

senses.title: Very poor in quality
senses.definition: used informally of something of very low quality or performance
senses.definitionCN: 口语中形容质量或表现极差
senses.example: This useless little fan does not cool the room at all.
senses.exampleCN: 这台破小风扇根本吹不凉屋子。
senses.why: Anything that fails to perform gets the label by a short step, and the word becomes ordinary slang for shoddy things.
senses.whyCN: 做不好事的东西很容易就被贴上这个标签，于是它也成了口语里形容蹩脚货的常用词。

senses.title: Unable to help or cope
senses.definition: describing a person who cannot help or deal with a situation
senses.definitionCN: 形容一个人帮不上忙、应付不了局面
senses.example: He felt useless while she packed for the move alone.
senses.exampleCN: 她一个人收拾搬家的东西时，他觉得很帮不上忙。
senses.why: A person whose hands cannot change things is like a broken tool, which is why the word also describes helpless feeling.
senses.whyCN: 一个人的手改变不了局面，就同一件坏工具无异；这层「感到无能为力」的用法由此而来。

intro.en: The native suffix -less, meaning without, added to the borrowed verb use; a plain negative compound.
intro.cn: 本土后缀 -less（意为「没有」）加在借入动词 use 之上，是一个直白的否定复合词。

items.en: The suffix -leas meant without or free from, as in homeless and hopeless.
items.cn: 后缀 -leas 意为「没有、免于」，如 homeless 与 hopeless 中的用法。

items.en: The base verb descends from uti and its participle usus, a using.
items.cn: 词基动词可溯至 uti 及其分词 usus，意为「使用」。

items.en: User and usé carried the verb through French into English.
items.cn: user 与 usé 把这个动词经法语带入英语。

items.en: Use joins the suffix so that useless names what has no use at all.
items.cn: use 与后缀结合，useless 便用来指毫无用处之物。

items.en: The sense widens to hopeless efforts and then to anything of poor quality.
items.cn: 词义扩大到徒劳的努力，继而扩展到任何质量低劣的东西。

note.en: The look-alike group is the same use stem with its negative suffix, and the near-meaning group lines up words for things that fail to work.
note.cn: 形近组是同一 use 词干加否定后缀，近义组则把「不起作用」一类词排成一列。

entries.definition: helpful for a purpose
without any result
to employ for a purpose
having no home
not producing the wanted result
having no value at all
completely without result
easy and useful to use

normalIntro.en: Use plus -less: without any use, and by a short step without any point.
normalIntro.cn: use 加 -less：没有用处，再往前一步就成了毫无意义。

normal.en: The pair useful and useless differ only in the suffix.
normal.cn: useful 与 useless 的区别只在那一个后缀上。

normal.en: Worse than useless means harmful as well as pointless.
normal.cn: worse than useless 指不但无用还有害。

normal.en: Uselessness is the noun, uselessly the adverb.
normal.cn: 名词是 uselessness，副词是 uselessly。

normal.en: The same -less pattern gives hopeless and careless.
normal.cn: hopeless、careless 走的是同一个 -less 模式。

normal.en: Feel useless describes a person, not a thing.
normal.cn: feel useless 描述的是人，而不是物。

abstract.en: Picture an umbrella whose ribs snap in the first gust of wind.
abstract.cn: 想象一把伞在第一阵风里就折断伞骨。

abstract.en: Hear yourself shouting advice that no one can hear.
abstract.cn: 听自己喊出的建议，没人听得见。

abstract.en: Hold a watch that has stopped at the same minute for years.
abstract.cn: 握着一只多年来始终停在同一分钟的表。

examples.en: Without a charger, the laptop is useless on the road.
examples.cn: 没有充电器，这台笔记本在路上派不上用场。

examples.en: Complaining after the decision proved a useless effort.
examples.cn: 决定之后再去抱怨，成了徒劳的力气。

examples.en: This useless pair of scissors cannot even cut paper.
examples.cn: 这把破剪刀连纸都剪不动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「优是劣」——表面看着优，一上手才发现是劣等货，全不管用。

root: 本土否定后缀 -less（没有）加动词 use（拉丁语 uti / usus，经古法语 user），义为「毫无用处」

sensesIntro.en: The core without any use spreads to efforts that change nothing, to shoddy goods, and to a person who cannot help.
sensesIntro.cn: 「毫无用处」这个核心扩展到改变不了局面的努力、粗劣的物品以及帮不上忙的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an umbrella with broken ribs in a downpour.
core.cn: 核心意象：倾盆大雨里一把断了伞骨的伞。

branches.en: The tool branch: it cannot do what it was made for.
branches.cn: 工具分支：它做不到自己该做的事。

branches.en: The effort branch: actions that leave the world unchanged.
branches.cn: 努力分支：行动过后局面毫无变化。

branches.en: The quality branch: shoddy goods in everyday speech.
branches.cn: 质量分支：口语里形容蹩脚货。

branches.en: The person branch: hands that can do nothing here.
branches.cn: 人身分支：一双手在此地帮不上任何忙。

branches.en: The judgement branch: no use and no effect are one verdict.
branches.cn: 评判分支：没用与无效其实是同一个判词。

intro.en: A negating Germanic suffix on a borrowed verb: without any use.
intro.cn: 日耳曼语否定后缀加在借入动词上：一点用处也没有。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Latin uti and its participle usus; the negative suffix itself is not Latin but native English.
latinIntro.cn: 词干是拉丁语 uti 及其分词 usus；否定后缀本身并非拉丁语，而是英语本土成分。

items.example: Use the back door, not the front.
Uselessness is the state of being useless.
He uselessly tried to fix it.
A user is a person who uses.

items.structure: base noun in the same pattern
items.exampleCN: hopeless 用的是同一个后缀。

items.structure: base noun in the same pattern
items.exampleCN: careless 同样展示了 -less 的用法。

definition_zh: 农业的；农学的；耕种的；农田的
definition_en: relating to farming, to the science of farming, or to land used for growing crops
core_image: 犁铧翻开泥土，一条直直的垄沟伸向远处
scene: 天还没亮，收割机就开进了麦田，车灯照着一行行麦茬。 The village depends on agricultural work that begins before sunrise.
sceneCN: 这里 agricultural 是「农业的」（第 1 个义项：与耕作、畜牧相关的）；句意为这个村子依靠天不亮就开始的农活为生。

pos.zh: 形容词：农业的；农学的；耕种的

derivatives.zh: 去掉形容词后缀得到的基础名词，义为「农业；农学」
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「在农业方面」
由本词加后缀 -ist 构成，义为「农学家；务农者」

senses.title: Relating to farming
senses.definition: relating to the growing of crops and the raising of animals for food
senses.definitionCN: 与种植作物、饲养食用动物相关的
senses.example: The village depends on agricultural work that begins before sunrise.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子依靠天不亮就开始的农活为生。
senses.why: The adjective simply attaches the whole activity of farming to any noun that follows it.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是把耕作这一整件事附加到它后面的名词上。

senses.title: Relating to the science of farming
senses.definition: relating to the academic study of farming methods and soils
senses.definitionCN: 与农作方法与土壤的学术研究相关的
senses.example: She is doing agricultural research on drought-resistant wheat.
senses.exampleCN: 她在做抗旱小麦的农业研究。
senses.why: Once farming becomes a subject taught in universities, its adjective also names the research side.
senses.whyCN: 一旦耕作成为大学里讲授的学科，这个形容词也用来指研究的那一面。

senses.title: Involving cultivation of the soil
senses.definition: involving the actual tilling and working of land
senses.definitionCN: 涉及实际翻耕与打理土地的
senses.example: Most families here have an agricultural life rather than an industrial one.
senses.exampleCN: 这里多数家庭过的是务农生活，而不是工业生活。
senses.why: Latina cultura meant tending, and the adjective keeps that hands-in-the-soil sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 cultura 意为「照料」，这个形容词保留了双手沾泥的那层意思。

senses.title: Of land used for crops
senses.definition: describing land or areas set aside for crops or pasture
senses.definitionCN: 描述专门用于种植或放牧的土地与区域
senses.example: Half of the region is agricultural land and the rest is forest.
senses.exampleCN: 这个地区一半是农田，其余是森林。
senses.why: Land itself can be labelled by what it is used for, so the adjective moves from activity to territory.
senses.whyCN: 土地本身可以按用途被命名，于是这个形容词从活动转到了地界。

intro.en: Agricultural is an English adjective on agriculture, whose two Latin halves mean field and tending.
intro.cn: agricultural 是在 agriculture 之上构成的英语形容词，而后者的两个拉丁成分意为「田地」与「照料」。

items.en: Ager meant a field or open land, and it is the first half of the word.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ager 意为「田地、开阔地」，是这个词的前半。

items.en: Cultura meant tending, cultivation, and later also the training of mind; here it keeps the farming sense.
items.cn: cultura 意为「照料、耕作」，后来也指心智的培养；在此保留农耕义。

items.en: The compound agricultura named the cultivation of fields, and English took it as agriculture in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 复合词 agricultura 指田地的耕作，英语十六世纪借入为 agriculture。

items.en: The adjective agricultural was formed with -al as farming became a subject of policy and science. Exact first dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 随着农业成为政策与科学研究的对象，形容词 agricultural 由 -al 构成。确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The adjective now covers farming as work, as science, and as a use of land.
items.cn: 如今这个形容词覆盖农业作为劳动、作为科学，以及作为土地用途三个方面。

note.en: The look-alike group is the agriculture family; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for country life and cultivation.
note.cn: 形近组是 agriculture 词族；近义组收描述乡村生活与耕作的其他形容词。

entries.definition: The noun for farming and for the science that studies it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「农业、农学」，是本词的基础形式。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning in farming terms or from a farming point of view.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在农业方面」，由本词加后缀构成。

entries.definition: A person who studies or practises farming as a profession.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「农学家、务农者」，由本词加后缀构成。

entries.definition: Relating to land ownership and rural society, rather than to farming technique.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「土地的、农耕社会的」，侧重土地制度而非耕作技术。

entries.definition: Relating to the countryside, including villages and life outside cities.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「乡村的」，涵盖村庄与城市之外的生活。

entries.definition: The everyday noun and modifier for the work of growing crops and keeping animals.
entries.definitionCN: 名词兼修饰语，义为「务农、耕作」，是最日常的说法。

entries.definition: Relating to garden cultivation, a narrower field than agriculture.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「园艺的」，范围比农业更窄，专指园圃栽培。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two Latin halves of the word and the phrases it appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用这个词的两个拉丁成分，以及它实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Ager is a field and cultura is tending, so agricultural means field-tending.
normal.cn: ager 是田地，cultura 是照料，所以 agricultural 就是「照料田地」。

normal.en: Agriculture is the noun; agricultural is what you call anything that belongs to it.
normal.cn: agriculture 是名词；凡属于它的事物，就用 agricultural 来形容。

normal.en: Agricultural land is land earmarked for crops or pasture.
normal.cn: agricultural land 是划给作物或牧场的土地。

normal.en: Agricultural science is the university side of the same activity.
normal.cn: agricultural science 是同一件事在大学里的那一面。

normal.en: Cultura also gives culture, which is the tending of minds instead of fields.
normal.cn: cultura 还生出 culture，那是照料心智而非田地。

abstract.en: Picture a plough blade opening the soil and a straight furrow running to the horizon.
abstract.cn: 想象犁铧翻开泥土，一条笔直的垄沟伸向天边。

abstract.en: Follow the furrow and it passes a laboratory, a policy office, and a land register.
abstract.cn: 沿着这条垄沟走，它会经过一间实验室、一个政策办公室和一本土地登记册。

abstract.en: The same line is work, study and territory at once.
abstract.cn: 同一条线同时是劳动、学问与地界。

examples.en: The village depends on agricultural work that begins before sunrise.
examples.cn: 这个村子依靠天不亮就开始的农活为生。

examples.en: Half of the region is agricultural land and the rest is forest.
examples.cn: 这个地区一半是农田，其余是森林。

examples.en: She is doing agricultural research on drought-resistant wheat.
examples.cn: 她在做抗旱小麦的农业研究。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿哥，犁扣」——阿哥把犁扣在田里：农业的

root: 拉丁语 ager「田地」加 cultura「照料、耕作」构成 agricultura「耕作田地」，英语十六世纪借入为 agriculture，十八世纪再加形容词后缀 -al 构成 agricultural；cultura 也是 culture 的来源。

sensesIntro.en: The four senses apply one adjective to four sides of the same activity: the work itself, the science of it, the labour of tilling, and the land it uses.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项把同一个形容词用到同一件事的四个侧面：农活本身、研究它的学问、翻土劳作，以及它所占的土地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plough blade opens the soil and a straight furrow runs towards the horizon.
core.cn: 核心意象：犁铧翻开泥土，一条笔直的垄沟伸向天边。

branches.en: THE WORK: the adjective names everything that belongs to growing crops and keeping animals.
branches.cn: 劳动线：这个形容词指一切与种植和饲养相关的事物。

branches.en: THE STUDY: the same activity becomes a university subject with its own research.
branches.cn: 学问线：同一件事变成大学里的一门学科，拥有自己的研究。

branches.en: THE HANDS: cultura keeps the sense of actual tending, hands in the soil.
branches.cn: 双手线：cultura 保留实际照料的意思，双手沾着泥土。

branches.en: THE GROUND: land is labelled by the use it is put to.
branches.cn: 土地线：土地按用途被命名。

branches.en: THE BASE: both rest on the same Latin pair, field plus tending.
branches.cn: 根基线：两者都建立在同一对拉丁成分上，即田地加照料。

intro.en: Agricultural combines a Latin compound noun with the English adjective suffix -al.
intro.cn: agricultural 把拉丁复合名词与英语形容词后缀 -al 组合在一起。

latinIntro.en: Ager, cultura and agricultura are all recorded, so nothing in this entry is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: ager、cultura 与 agricultura 均有记录，本条目的成分都不是重构形式。

items.example: Ager is the first half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: ager 是这个复合词的前半。

items.example: Cultura also gives the English word culture.
items.exampleCN: cultura 还生出英语词 culture。

items.example: It appears in agronomy and agrochemical.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 agronomy 与 agrochemical 中。

items.example: The map marks all agricultural land in green.
items.exampleCN: 地图把农业用地都标成绿色。

derivatives.zh: 去掉形容词后缀得到的基础名词，义为「农业」
由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「在农业方面」
由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「农学家」

definition_en: to control an activity by official rules; to adjust a machine or a process so that it stays steady; to keep a feeling or an amount within limits
core_image: 墙上的恒温器被手指轻轻拧动一格
scene: 墙上的恒温器被手指轻轻拧动一格，暖气随之安静下来。 A small device regulates the temperature of the tank.
sceneCN: 这里 regulates 是 regulate 的第三人称单数，取「调节」（第 2 个义项：调整设备使保持稳定）；句意为一个小装置调节着水箱的温度。画面里可留意：被拧动一格的恒温器、安静下来的暖气。

derivatives.zh: 规章；管理；调节
管理者；调节器
监管的；管理的

senses.title: To control by rules
senses.definition: to control an activity or a business through official rules
senses.definitionCN: 通过正式规章控制某项活动或行业
senses.example: The agency regulates the sale of medicines.
senses.exampleCN: 这个机构监管药品的销售。
senses.why: The word is built on the Latin word for a rule, so the first sense is simply to apply a rule to something.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在拉丁语表「规则」的词上，所以第一义就是把规则施加于某物。

senses.title: To adjust for steadiness
senses.definition: to adjust a machine or a process so that it stays at the right level
senses.definitionCN: 调整机器或过程，使其保持在合适的水平
senses.example: A small device regulates the temperature of the tank.
senses.exampleCN: 一个小装置调节着水箱的温度。
senses.why: A thermostat applies a rule to heat: it measures, compares, and corrects, which is regulation without paper.
senses.whyCN: 恒温器把一条规则用于热量：测量、比较、修正，这是没有纸面的管理。

senses.title: To keep within limits
senses.definition: to hold a feeling, an amount, or a habit within reasonable limits
senses.definitionCN: 把情绪、数量或习惯控制在合理范围内
senses.example: He learned to regulate his temper in front of the class.
senses.exampleCN: 他学会在全班面前控制自己的脾气。
senses.why: Governing a state and governing a temper use the same verb, because both keep something from running past its limit.
senses.whyCN: 治理国家与控制脾气用同一个动词，因为两者都是不让某物越过限度。

intro.en: Regulate is to apply a rule: the Latin noun for a straight rod became a verb of controlling and adjusting.
intro.cn: regulate 就是「施加规则」：拉丁语中表直尺的名词，变成了表控制与调节的动词。

items.en: Regere meant to rule and keep straight, the root of the whole family.
items.cn: regere 意为统治与使直，是整个词族的根。

items.en: Regula was a straight rod for measuring, and so a rule or a standard.
items.cn: regula 是一根用来量度的直尺，因此也指规则或标准。

items.en: Regulare meant to direct by a rule or to set in order.
items.cn: regulare 意为按规则指导或使之有序。

items.en: Regulator named one who sets things in order, and the word passed into technical use.
items.cn: regulator 指使事物有序的人，这个词后来进入技术领域。

items.en: With machines, regulate came to mean keeping a process at a steady level automatically.
items.cn: 到了机器时代，regulate 开始表示自动把某个过程维持在稳定水平。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the same rule family; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of controlling and adjusting.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「规则」词族的词；近义组收表示控制与调整的动词。

entries.definition: An official rule.
A body or device that regulates.
Even and usual.
To direct or hold in check.
To change slightly for a better fit.
To rule or influence.
To make less extreme.

normalIntro.en: The verb puts a rule to work: on a market, on a machine, or on a temper.
normalIntro.cn: 这个动词让一条规则开始工作：作用于市场、机器，或者脾气。

normal.en: Regula is a rule, and regulate is to make a rule act.
normal.cn: regula 是规则，regulate 就是让规则起作用。

normal.en: A thermostat regulates heat the way a teacher regulates a class.
normal.cn: 恒温器调节热量，就像老师管理班级。

normal.en: Strictly regulated industries answer to a public body.
normal.cn: strictly regulated 的行业要向公共机构负责。

normal.en: To regulate your temper is to keep it inside a line.
normal.cn: regulate your temper 就是把脾气关在一条线内。

normal.en: The noun is regulation, the device a regulator.
normal.cn: 名词是 regulation，装置是 regulator。

abstract.en: To regulate is to decide where the limit lies, and then hold it.
abstract.cn: 调节就是先决定限度在哪里，然后守住它。

abstract.en: A machine that regulates itself is trusted to have no moods.
abstract.cn: 能自我调节的机器被相信是没有情绪的。

abstract.en: Self-regulation is the hardest kind, because no one else holds the rod.
abstract.cn: 自律是最难的一种，因为尺子不在别人手里。

examples.en: A small device regulates the temperature of the tank.
examples.cn: 一个小装置调节着水箱的温度。

examples.en: The agency regulates the sale of medicines.
examples.cn: 这个机构监管药品的销售。

examples.en: He learned to regulate his temper in front of the class.
examples.cn: 他学会在全班面前控制自己的脾气。

dict_mnemonic.text: regula（规则、直尺）加 ate（动词尾）：用规则去管一个行业，用尺子去调一个温度，用尺度去控一份情绪。

root: 拉丁 regere（统治、使直）→ regula（直尺、规则）→ regulare（按规则指导）→ 英语 regulate；同族有 regulation、regulator、regulatory，形近的 regular 也出自 regula。

sensesIntro.en: The core is applying a rule; the senses move from official control, to the automatic adjustment of a machine, to keeping a feeling in bounds.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「施加规则」；义项从官方的管制，到对机器的自动调节，再到把情绪约束在界内。

core.cn: 核心意象：墙上的恒温器被手指轻轻拧动一格。

branches.cn: 保持同一温度的水箱

branches.en: a pause before an angry answer
branches.cn: 发火之前的一次停顿

branches.en: a rule written and a rule built in
branches.cn: 写在纸上的规则与装进机器里的规则

branches.en: a temperature and a temper both held
branches.cn: 被稳住的温度与被压住的脾气

latinIntro.en: The base is regula, a rule; the verb regulare means to set by rule, and -ate forms the English verb.

definition_en: able to speak a language smoothly, or moving and expressed with ease
core_image: 一个人说着外语，句子像水一样连续不断地流出来
scene: 她说一口流利的英语。 She speaks fluent English.
sceneCN: 这里 fluent 是「流利的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她说一口流利的英语。

derivatives.zh: 流利；流畅
流利地

senses.title: Smooth speech
senses.definition: able to speak a language easily and well
senses.definitionCN: 能轻松而出色地说一门语言
senses.example: She speaks fluent English.
senses.exampleCN: 她说一口流利的英语。
senses.why: This is the most common modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代最常见的义项。

senses.title: Smooth expression
senses.definition: expressed in a smooth, natural way
senses.definitionCN: 以流畅自然的方式表达的
senses.example: His writing is clear and fluent.
senses.exampleCN: 他的文章清晰流畅。
senses.why: The idea of smooth flow extends to writing.
senses.whyCN: 流畅的概念延伸到写作。

senses.title: Skilled movement
senses.definition: moving with ease and skill
senses.definitionCN: 轻松而熟练地移动
senses.example: The dancer made fluent movements.
senses.exampleCN: 舞者的动作流畅熟练。
senses.why: Smooth language and smooth motion share one image.
senses.whyCN: 流畅的语言与流畅的动作共享一个意象。

intro.en: Fluent comes from Latin fluere, to flow.
intro.cn: fluent 来自拉丁语 fluere，意为流动。

items.en: Fluere meant to flow like water.
items.cn: fluere 意为像水一样流动。

items.en: Fluens described something flowing freely.
items.cn: fluens 形容自由流动的东西。

items.en: Fluent described smooth, flowing speech.
items.cn: fluent 形容流畅的言语。

items.en: Fluent extended to writing and movement.
items.cn: fluent 扩展到写作与动作。

items.en: Fluency became a goal for language learners.
items.cn: fluency 成为语言学习者的目标。

note.en: Fluent is compared with similar-looking words and with words for ease and flow.
note.cn: 把 fluent 与形近词以及表示轻松和流动的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Fluent speech flows like water: no bumps, no stops.
normalIntro.cn: fluent 的语言像水一样流：不磕绊、不停顿。

normal.en: She is fluent in English.

normal.en: He gave a fluent speech.
normal.cn: 他做了一次流畅的演讲。

normal.en: Her fluent French impressed us.

normal.en: Practice makes you more fluent.

normal.en: The dancer moved in a fluent way.

abstract.en: Fluency hides years of practice.

abstract.en: Water and words both find the easy path.
abstract.cn: 水与话语都会找到顺畅的路径。

abstract.en: A fluent line never shows where it stopped.
abstract.cn: 流畅的线条从不停下来给人看。

root: 源自拉丁语 fluere（流动），核心义「像水一样顺畅地流出」。

sensesIntro.en: Fluent means smooth in speech, smooth in expression, or skilled in movement.
sensesIntro.cn: fluent 意为语言流利的、表达流畅的或动作熟练的。

core.en: Words or movement that flow without effort.

branches.en: Speech that runs like water.

branches.en: Writing with no rough joins.

branches.en: Skill makes both words and bodies flow.

intro.en: Fluent forms a family of flow and smoothness words.

latinIntro.en: Fluent contains Latin fluere, to flow, a root shared with fluid and flush.

definition_en: to increase or improve something
core_image: 一只手把数字往上推
scene: 新广告让销量明显上升。 The new advert boosted sales by a third.

derivatives.zh: 助推器；支持者

senses.title: To increase or improve
senses.definition: to make something rise in amount or quality
senses.definitionCN: 使数量或质量上升
senses.example: The new advert boosted sales by a third.
senses.exampleCN: 新广告让销量提高了三分之一。
senses.why: This is the main modern sense, from a push from below.
senses.whyCN: 这是主要的现代义项，来自从下面往上推的动作。

senses.title: An act of help
senses.definition: something that gives help or encouragement
senses.definitionCN: 给予帮助或鼓励的事物
senses.example: The win gave the team a boost.
senses.exampleCN: 这场胜利给了球队一股推动力。
senses.why: A push upward is felt as help, so the noun names that help.
senses.whyCN: 向上的一推被感受为帮助，名词便指这种帮助。

senses.title: To raise confidence

senses.definitionCN: 使某人更有信心
senses.example: Praise can boost a child's confidence.

senses.why: Confidence is pictured as something that can be lifted higher.

definition_zh: 补丁；小块土地；斑块；修补；软件补丁
definition_en: a small piece of material sewn over a hole, a small area of ground or a spot of different colour, the act of mending with such a piece, or a small software fix
core_image: 膝盖破口上缝着的一方深色布片
scene: 旧屋的窗纸破了一角，老人从针线盒里剪下一块深色布。 She sewed a patch over the hole in his jacket.
sceneCN: 这里的 patch 是「补丁、补片」（第 1 个义项：缝在破口上的那块布）；句意是她在他外套的破洞上缝了一块补丁。图中可辨识物件：针线盒、深色布片、磨破的外套。

pos.zh: 补丁；小块土地；斑块；软件补丁

derivatives.zh: 由 patch 加 -y 构成，义为「斑驳的；时好时坏的」
由 patch 与 work 复合而成，义为「拼布；拼凑之物」
由 patchy 加 -ness 构成，义为「不均；零散」

senses.title: A piece of cloth sewn over a hole
senses.definition: a small piece of material fixed over a hole or a worn place in clothes or fabric
senses.definitionCN: 缝在衣服或织物破洞、磨损处上方的一小块材料
senses.example: He wore a leather patch on the elbow of his coat.
senses.exampleCN: 他外套的肘部缝着一块皮补丁。
senses.why: Patch first named a piece cut to size, so the noun starts from the shape of the hole: what matters is the piece that fits it, not the mending itself.
senses.whyCN: patch 最初指剪好尺寸的一块东西，所以名词的起点是破洞的形状：关键是那块刚好合上的布，而不是缝补这件事。

senses.title: A small piece of ground
senses.definition: a small area of ground, especially one used for growing vegetables or flowers
senses.definitionCN: 一小块地面，尤指用来种菜或种花的
senses.example: They kept a vegetable patch behind the kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在厨房后面留了一小块菜地。
senses.why: Since a patch is a piece marked off from a larger surface, ground can be divided the same way, and a garden plot becomes a patch of earth.
senses.whyCN: 既然 patch 是从更大表面上划出的一小块，土地也能这样划分，于是一畦菜地就成了「一块」地。

senses.title: A spot of different colour
senses.definition: a small area of a surface that differs in colour or texture from the rest of it
senses.definitionCN: 表面上与其余部分颜色或质地不同的一小块区域
senses.example: A pale patch spread across the damp wall.
senses.exampleCN: 潮湿的墙上洇开了一块浅色斑。
senses.why: The same idea of a local piece applies to colour: a patch is where one shade covers a small area instead of the whole surface.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「局部一块」的念头也适用于颜色：patch 就是某一种色调只盖住一小片、而不是整面墙的地方。

senses.title: To mend with a piece
senses.definition: to cover a hole or worn place with a piece of material
senses.definitionCN: 用一块材料把破洞或磨损处盖住
senses.example: He patched the torn sail with a strip of canvas before the wind rose.
senses.exampleCN: 起风之前，他用一条帆布把破了的船帆补上。
senses.why: The verb is simply the noun put to work: to patch is to do what a patch does, laying one piece over a gap.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是把名词拿来用：to patch 就是做一块补丁所做的事，把一片东西盖在缺口上。

senses.title: A small software fix
senses.definition: a small piece of software added to a program to correct a fault or close a security hole
senses.definitionCN: 加在程序上的一小段软件，用来纠正故障或堵住安全漏洞
senses.example: The company released a patch for the security flaw within a day.
senses.exampleCN: 公司在一天之内就发布了修补这个安全漏洞的补丁。
senses.why: A flaw in a program is imagined as a hole, and the fix is imagined as a piece laid over it, so the cloth word moves into computing intact.
senses.whyCN: 程序里的缺陷被想象成一个洞，修好的办法被想象成盖上去的一片东西，于是这个缝补的词原封不动地走进了计算机领域。

intro.en: Patch is first recorded in Middle English as pacche, and its origin is uncertain; a link with Old French pieche, the ancestor of piece, is often suggested but cannot be proved.
intro.cn: patch 最早以 pacche 的形式见于中古英语，来源不确定；人们常说它与古法语 pieche（piece 的前身）有关，但无法证实。

items.en: The word appears in the fourteenth century as pacche, naming a piece of cloth set over a hole; no earlier form is securely recorded.
items.cn: 这个词在十四世纪以 pacche 的形式出现，指盖在破洞上的一块布；更早的形式没有可靠记录。

items.en: One common view connects it with Old French pieche, a piece or fragment, which would make it a distant relative of piece.
items.cn: 一种常见的看法把它与古法语 pieche（一块、碎片）联系起来，若成立，它便是 piece 的远亲。

items.en: Other scholars point to Low German and Middle Dutch words for a clout or a rag, suggesting the word was borrowed from trade speech rather than from French.
items.cn: 另一些学者指向低地德语与中古荷兰语中表示「破布、补块」的词，认为它来自商贸用语，而非来自法语。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the word also named a plot of ground, and the verb patched appeared beside the noun.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，这个词也能指一块地，动词 patched 也已在名词旁边出现。

items.en: Modern English keeps the cloth, land and colour senses, adds the computing sense in the twentieth century, and forms patchy and patchwork.
items.cn: 现代英语保留布料、土地与颜色三个义项，二十世纪又添上计算机义，并造出 patchy 与 patchwork。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the English words built on patch and two borrowings that only share its sound; the near-meaning group gathers words for mending and for small areas.
note.cn: 形近组收由 patch 构成的英语词，以及两个只是读音相近的外来词；近义组收表示「修补」与「小块区域」的词。
