normalIntro.en: Patch has no classical root to lean on, so its hooks come from the shape of a piece laid over a gap and from the English words built on it.
normalIntro.cn: patch 没有可依托的古典词根，所以记忆钩子来自「一片东西盖在缺口上」的形状，以及由它构成的英语词。

normal.en: Patchy is patch plus -y: something covered with patches looks uneven, so the adjective came to mean good in some places and bad in others.
normal.cn: patchy 是 patch 加 -y：盖满补丁的东西看上去不均匀，于是这个形容词引申为「有些地方好、有些地方差」。

normal.en: Patchwork is patch plus work: a whole surface made by sewing many separate pieces into one.
normal.cn: patchwork 是 patch 加 work：把许多分开的布片缝成一整块表面。

normal.en: Patch up keeps the cloth image for human affairs: to patch things up is to cover the tear in a relationship, not to weave new cloth.
normal.cn: patch up 把缝布的画面用到了人事上：修补关系是盖住那道裂口，而不是重新织一块布。

normal.en: The plural is patches with -es, because English adds -es after the ch sound.
normal.cn: 复数是 patches，加 -es，因为英语在 ch 音之后要加 -es。

normal.en: A software patch borrows the same picture: a small piece laid over a hole until a new version can replace the whole garment.
normal.cn: 软件补丁借用的是同一幅画面：先用一小片盖住漏洞，等新版本再把整件衣服换掉。

abstract.en: A patch never pretends the tear did not happen; it makes the damage visible and still keeps the garment in use.
abstract.cn: 补丁从不假装破口没发生过；它让损伤看得见，却仍让这件衣服继续可穿。

abstract.en: Because a patch is local, it teaches a modest kind of repair: fix the small place, leave the rest alone, and accept that the result will show.
abstract.cn: 因为补丁是局部的，它教的是一种克制的修补：只处理那一小处，别处不动，也接受修补的痕迹会留下。

abstract.en: Calling a plot of land a patch says that ownership is also a matter of drawing a boundary around a small piece of the earth.
abstract.cn: 把一块地叫作 patch，等于说「拥有」也是在土地上圈出一小片边界。

examples.en: He wore a leather patch on the elbow of his coat.
examples.cn: 他外套的肘部缝着一块皮补丁。

examples.en: They kept a vegetable patch behind the kitchen.
examples.cn: 他们在厨房后面留了一小块菜地。

examples.en: The company released a patch for the security flaw within a day.
examples.cn: 公司在一天之内就发布了修补这个安全漏洞的补丁。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕扯」——衣服破了个口，怕再扯大，就先缝上一块布；记住 patch 是补丁，也指一小块地。

root: 中古英语 pacche 首见，来源不确定；一般认为可能与古法语 pieche（一块，piece 的前身）有关，也有人联系低地德语或中古荷兰语中表示「破布、补块」的词；没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a piece cut to fit a gap; the senses divide into the cloth piece, the piece of ground, the colour spot, the act of mending and the software fix.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是剪好尺寸、正好盖住缺口的一片东西；义项按「布料补片」「一块地」「色斑」「缝补动作」「软件补丁」分出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dark square of cloth stitched over a tear at the knee.
core.cn: 核心意象：膝盖破口上缝着的一方深色布片。

branches.en: a square of cloth stitched to a knee
branches.cn: 缝在膝盖上的一方布

branches.en: a coat sleeve worn thin at the elbow
branches.cn: 肘部磨薄的衣袖

branches.en: a vegetable plot behind a kitchen
branches.cn: 厨房后的一小块菜地

branches.en: a pale patch spreading on a damp wall
branches.cn: 潮墙上洇开的浅色斑

branches.en: a torn sail covered, then a program repaired
branches.cn: 先是补好的破帆，后是修好的程序

intro.en: Patch carries no distinctive prefix or suffix of its own, so these entries show the English endings, compounds and phrases built around it.
intro.cn: patch 本身没有标志性的前缀或后缀，因此这里列出围绕它构成的英语词尾、复合词与短语。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate can be shown for patch; the Old French link is only a hypothesis, so no Latin entry is listed here.
latinIntro.cn: patch 找不到可靠的拉丁同族词；与古法语的关联只是假说，因此这里不列拉丁词条。

items.meaning: a piece set over a hole

items.meaningCN: 过去式与过去分词词尾

items.meaning: a small fix added to a program
items.meaningCN: 加在程序上的小型修补

definition_en: to break down food in the body, to take in information, or a short summary of a longer text
core_image: 一大块面包泡在温水里，慢慢散成看不见的细末
scene: 他饭后靠在椅背上，等胃把那顿硬面包慢慢化开。 It takes hours to digest such a heavy meal.
sceneCN: 这里 digest 指「消化」（第 1 个义项：把食物分解吸收）；句意是这么油腻的一顿要几个小时才能消化。

derivatives.zh: 消化；消化能力
消化的
易消化的
消化不良

senses.title: To break down food
senses.definition: to change food in the body into something it can use
senses.definitionCN: 在体内把食物变成身体能用的东西
senses.example: Some people cannot digest milk easily.
senses.exampleCN: 有些人不容易消化牛奶。
senses.why: A large piece must become small before the body can take it.
senses.whyCN: 大块的东西必须先变碎，身体才拿得走。

senses.title: To take in ideas
senses.definition: to read or hear something and make it your own
senses.definitionCN: 读过或听过之后，把它变成自己的东西
senses.example: Give the class time to digest the new rule.
senses.exampleCN: 给学生一点时间消化这条新规则。
senses.why: The mind chews in the same slow way the stomach does.
senses.whyCN: 脑子咀嚼的节奏，和胃一样慢。

senses.title: A short version of a text
senses.definition: a small collection of the main points of longer writing
senses.definitionCN: 把较长文字的主要意思收成一小份
senses.example: The magazine prints a monthly digest of new research.
senses.exampleCN: 这本杂志每月印一份新研究摘要。
senses.why: What has been digested comes out shorter and easier to carry.
senses.whyCN: 被消化过的东西，出来时更短也更好带。

intro.en: Digest comes from Latin digerere, to carry apart, from dis-, apart, and gerere, to carry.
intro.cn: digest 来自拉丁语 digerere（分开搬运），由 dis-（分开）与 gerere（搬、带）构成。

items.en: Gerere meant to carry or to manage a burden.
items.cn: gerere 指搬运，也指料理一份负担。

items.en: Digerere meant to separate things and set them in order.
items.cn: digerere 指把东西分开，再排好顺序。

items.en: Medical writers used it for the body softening food.
items.cn: 医学作者用它形容身体把食物化开。

items.en: English digest covered food, and soon also books.
items.cn: 英语 digest 先指食物，很快也用于书。

items.en: The noun came to mean a compact collection of articles.
items.cn: 名词义后来指把文章收成一小册。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the gest- ending, while the meaning group covers absorbing, summarising and blending in.
note.cn: 形近组共用 gest 结尾，近义组则覆盖吸收、概括与融会。

entries.definition: to move away from the main subject while speaking
relating to the process of digesting food
easy for the body to break down
to take in liquid, energy or knowledge
a short account of the main points
to take in and make part of oneself
entries.definitionCN: 吸收并化为自身的一部分

normalIntro.en: These hooks go from bread softening in the stomach to a thick magazine folded into a thin summary.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从胃里化开的面包，走到一本厚杂志被折成一页薄摘要。

normal.en: The verb says dye-JEST; the noun says DYE-jest.
normal.cn: 动词重音在后，名词重音在前，意思也随之分工。

normal.en: The stomach digests food and the mind digests a chapter.
normal.cn: 胃消化食物，脑子消化一章书。

normal.en: A digest is what is left after all the chewing.
normal.cn: digest 是嚼完之后剩下的那一小份。

normal.en: Easy to digest is praise for soup and for prose.
normal.cn: easy to digest 既能夸汤，也能夸文章。

normal.en: Indigestion is the body refusing a hurried meal.
normal.cn: 消化不良，是身体拒绝一顿太急的饭。

abstract.en: Picture a slice of bread slowly losing its shape in water.
abstract.cn: 想象一片面包在水里慢慢失去形状。

abstract.en: Picture a thick book pressed down to ten thin pages.
abstract.cn: 想象一本厚书被压成十张薄纸。

abstract.en: Picture a reader nodding slowly as a hard idea settles.
abstract.cn: 想象一个难懂的念头落定，读者慢慢点头。

examples.en: He read the report and digested its main points.
examples.cn: 他读完报告，吸收了其中的要点。

examples.en: This soup is easy to digest.
examples.cn: 这种汤很容易消化。

examples.en: The digest arrives every Friday morning.
examples.cn: 这份文摘每周五早上送到。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 digest 记成「袋子嚼死它」：袋子里的东西一层层嚼碎，就是消化。

root: 来自拉丁语 digerere，由 dis-（分开）与 gerere（搬、带）构成，本义是把东西分开搬走、排好次序。医学上用它指身体把食物化开，于是有了「消化」；把厚材料化短，则有了「摘要」；把知识化进脑子，就是「理解吸收」。

sensesIntro.en: From food broken into pieces, to ideas taken in slowly, to a long text folded into a few pages.
sensesIntro.cn: 从被拆碎的食物，到慢慢吃进去的想法，再到把长文折成几页。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a large solid piece slowly breaking into fine parts.
core.cn: 核心意象：一大块结实的东西，慢慢散成细末。

branches.en: The first sense is the work of the stomach.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是胃干的活。

branches.en: The second sense hands the same work to the mind.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把同样的活交给脑子。

branches.en: The third sense keeps only the reduced result.
branches.cn: 第三个义项只留下被压缩后的成果。

branches.en: Body and mind both need time before they can use what comes in.
branches.cn: 身体和脑子都需要时间，才能用上进来的东西。

branches.en: A summary is proof that someone has already digested the text.
branches.cn: 摘要就是有人已经把全文消化过的证据。

intro.en: Digest gathers the gest- family, words about carrying, ordering and breaking down.
intro.cn: digest 聚起 gest 一族词，围绕搬运、排序与分解。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin gerere, to carry, with dis- meaning apart.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 gerere（搬、带），前缀 dis- 表示分开。

items.meaning: to break down and take in
the process of breaking down food

items.example: The digestive system is slow at night.
items.exampleCN: 夜里消化系统运转得慢。

items.example: He took a pill for indigestion.
items.exampleCN: 他吃了一片治消化不良的药。

items.example: The food was fully digested by noon.
items.exampleCN: 到中午食物已完全消化。

items.meaning: in the middle of breaking down
items.exampleCN: 蛇在消化时会静卧不动。

definition_en: agreement with a rule, wish or fact, chiefly in the phrase in accordance with
core_image: 施工图纸旁边摊着安全规范，两条线被逐条对齐
scene: 施工队进场前，先把图纸摊开，逐条对照当地的安全规范。 All work was carried out in accordance with safety rules.
sceneCN: 这里的 accordance 指「依照」（第 2 个义项：以某项规定为行动依据）；句意是所有工作都依照安全规程进行。

pos.zh: 一致；依照（常用于 in accordance with）

derivatives.zh: 义为「协议；一致」
义为「因此；相应地」

senses.title: Agreement in state
senses.definition: the state of agreeing with something or being consistent with it
senses.definitionCN: 与某事物相合、并不抵触的状态
senses.example: There is no accordance between the two reports.
senses.exampleCN: 这两份报告之间并不一致。
senses.why: The noun is accord plus -ance, naming the state rather than the act, so it describes two things resting in agreement.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词是 accord 加 -ance，指一种状态而不是动作，描述的是两样东西彼此相合地摆在一起。

senses.title: Acting by a rule
senses.definition: the relation of acting exactly as a rule or wish requires
senses.definitionCN: 完全按照某项规则或意愿行事的关系
senses.example: All work was carried out in accordance with safety rules.
senses.exampleCN: 所有工作都依照安全规程进行。
senses.why: In the fixed phrase in accordance with, the state of matching becomes the basis of action, so the word is read as according to.
senses.whyCN: 在固定短语 in accordance with 里，「相合」的状态成了行动的依据，于是这个词被理解为「按照」。

intro.en: The word is accord with a noun ending that turns agreement into a state.
intro.cn: 这个词是 accord 加上把「一致」变成状态的名词词尾。

items.en: cor meant heart, and ad cor meant to the heart.
items.cn: cor 意为心，ad cor 意为到心口。

items.en: acorder meant to bring into agreement.
items.cn: acorder 意为使一致。

items.en: accord named both harmony and a settlement.
items.cn: accord 既指和谐，也指和解。

items.en: -ance was added to name the state of being in accord.
items.cn: 加上 -ance 之后，用来指「处于一致之中」的状态。

items.en: the word now lives mainly inside in accordance with.
items.cn: 如今这个词主要活在 in accordance with 这个短语里。

note.en: The look-alike group is the accord family; the near-meaning group names conformity to rules.
note.cn: 形近组是 accord 词族；近义组表示对规则的遵循。

entries.definition: a formal agreement or harmony
in a way that follows from something
matching or in harmony
behaviour that follows accepted rules
the act of obeying a rule
the state of matching or consenting
a pleasing fit between parts
the quality of always matching

normalIntro.en: These hints follow accord and its root meaning heart.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条顺着 accord 与它「心」的词根。

normal.en: accordance is the state of being in accord, not the act of agreeing.
normal.cn: accordance 是「处于一致之中」的状态，不是「去同意」的动作。

normal.en: the phrase in accordance with is the one place the word is heard daily.
normal.cn: in accordance with 是这个词每天被听到的那一个位置。

normal.en: rules on one side and work on the other are laid line against line.
normal.cn: 一边是规程，一边是施工，要一条一条对齐。

normal.en: the -ance ending makes a condition out of the older noun.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ance 把较早的名词变成一种状态。

normal.en: acting in accordance with the law means the deed matches the text.
normal.cn: 依法行事，就是行为与条文对得上。

abstract.en: Picture a drawing set beside a rule book, edge to edge.
abstract.cn: 想象图纸与规程并排摊开、边对边。

abstract.en: See two rulers laid together with no gap showing.
abstract.cn: 想象两把尺子并在一起，中间没有缝。

abstract.en: Think of a stamp pressed exactly inside a marked square.
abstract.cn: 想象印章正好盖在框好的方格内。

examples.en: All work was carried out in accordance with safety rules.
examples.cn: 所有工作都依照安全规程进行。

examples.en: There is no accordance between the two reports.
examples.cn: 这两份报告之间并不一致。

examples.en: The payment was made in accordance with the contract.
examples.cn: 款项是依照合同支付的。

dict_mnemonic.text: accord（一致）+ -ance（状态）——处于一致之中的状态，就是 accordance；in accordance with 即「依照」。

root: accord 加名词后缀 -ance 构成，源自拉丁语 ad cor（到心口），本义「处于相合状态」，现代主要用于 in accordance with（依照）。

sensesIntro.en: The noun names a state of matching, and that state becomes the ground for action in one fixed phrase.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名词指一种相合的状态，而这一状态在一个固定短语里成了行动的依据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drawing laid edge to edge with a rule book.
core.cn: 核心意象：图纸与规程边对边摊开。

branches.en: two reports that show no gap between them
branches.cn: 两份报告之间看不出缝隙

branches.en: work done exactly as the rules describe
branches.cn: 完全照规程描述去做的工作

branches.en: a wish and a deed resting in agreement
branches.cn: 意愿与行为彼此相合

branches.en: a payment that follows the contract line by line
branches.cn: 逐条跟随合同的付款

branches.en: matching in state becomes matching in action
branches.cn: 状态上的相合，变成行动上的相合

intro.en: The word is an older noun of harmony with a state-naming suffix.
intro.cn: 这个词是表示和谐的旧名词加一个指状态的后缀。

latinIntro.en: The root cor, heart, also gives cordial and courage.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 cor（心）还给出 cordial 与 courage。

derivatives.zh: 义为「协议」
义为「因此」

definition_en: a form of a language spoken in one area or by one group of people
core_image: 同一条街两头的人，用不同腔调说同一个词
scene: 集市上卖菜的老人把「土豆」说成另一个音，年轻人听不太懂。 The dialect spoken in the valley has its own words for rain.
sceneCN: 这里 dialect 指「方言」（第 1 个义项：某一地区通行的语言变体）；句意是山谷里说的方言有自己一套表示雨的词。

derivatives.zh: 方言的
在方言方面
方言学
方言学家

senses.title: A regional form of a language
senses.definition: a form of a language spoken in one particular area
senses.definitionCN: 在某一特定地区通行的一种语言形式
senses.example: The dialect spoken in the valley has its own words for rain.
senses.exampleCN: 山谷里说的方言有自己一套表示雨的词。
senses.why: Every valley keeps its own small vocabulary for weather.
senses.whyCN: 每个山谷都为天气留着自己的一小套词。

senses.title: A group's way of speaking
senses.definition: the speech of a social group or trade rather than a whole region
senses.definitionCN: 某一社会群体或行业而非整个地区所说的语言
senses.example: The dock workers had a dialect full of sea words.
senses.exampleCN: 码头工人有一种满是海上词汇的土语。
senses.why: A trade grows its own words the way a garden grows its own weeds.
senses.whyCN: 一个行业长出自己的词，就像园子长出自己的草。

senses.title: A particular style of speech
senses.definition: a special way of speaking used by a group or in a piece of writing
senses.definitionCN: 某个群体或某篇作品里使用的特别说法
senses.example: The poem is written in the dialect of the streets.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗用的是街头那套用语。
senses.why: A style of speech is a costume a text can wear.
senses.whyCN: 一种说话方式，是文字可以穿上的戏服。

intro.en: Dialect comes from Greek dialektos, a conversation or the speech of a region, from dialegesthai, to talk with someone.
intro.cn: dialect 来自希腊语 dialektos（交谈、某地区的说话方式），源自动词 dialegesthai（与人交谈）。

items.en: Dialegesthai meant to talk something through with another person.
items.cn: dialegesthai 指与另一个人把话说透。

items.en: Dialektos named the speech of a particular place or group.
items.cn: dialektos 指某个地方或群体特有的说话方式。

items.en: Latin dialectus kept the sense of a local form of Greek.
items.cn: 拉丁语 dialectus 保留了「希腊语的地方变体」这一意思。

items.en: English dialect was used for regional forms of any language.
items.cn: 英语 dialect 用来指任何语言的地方变体。

items.en: Linguists now treat dialects as full systems, not errors.
items.cn: 如今语言学家把方言看作完整系统，而不是错误。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dia- opening, and the meaning group names accents, local speech and languages.
note.cn: 形近组共用 dia- 开头，近义组则指口音、本地话与语言。

entries.definition: belonging to a local form of speech
a conversation between people
reasoning through opposing ideas
entries.definitionCN: 通过对立观点推进的推理

entries.definition: the way a group pronounces words
entries.definitionCN: 一群人说词的发音方式

entries.definition: the everyday speech of ordinary people
a system of words used by a people
entries.definitionCN: 一个民族使用的词语系统

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with two accents on one street and end with a poem wearing the speech of the street.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从同一条街上的两种腔调开始，落到一首穿着街头用语的诗。

normal.en: Dialect began as the word for conversation, not for error.
normal.cn: dialect 最初是「交谈」的意思，并不是「错误」。

normal.en: A valley can put its own name on the rain.
normal.cn: 一个山谷，能给雨起自己的名字。

normal.en: Every trade carries a small dictionary in its pocket.
normal.cn: 每个行业的口袋里都装着一本小词典。

normal.en: An accent is how it sounds; a dialect is what it says.
normal.cn: 口音是听起来怎样，方言是说了些什么。

normal.en: Two villages, one language, and a fence of words between them.

senses.title: The treaty on paper: a formal agreement
senses.titleCN: 协议、议定书：写在纸上的正式约定
senses.definition: a formal agreement or treaty, especially one between states or organizations
senses.definitionCN: 正式的协议或条约，尤指国家或组织之间的
senses.example: The two governments signed a protocol on border patrols.
senses.exampleCN: 两国政府签署了一份关于边境巡逻的议定书。
senses.why: From the 1540s sense 'draft of a document, original of any writing', a protocol became the official record of a transaction. When that record is signed by friendly powers, the sheet of paper is the agreement itself.
senses.whyCN: 从 16 世纪 40 年代“文件草稿、任何文书的原件”这一义项起，protocol 成为交易的官方记录。当这份记录由友好国家签署，那张纸本身就是协议。

senses.title: The order of the room: diplomatic etiquette
senses.titleCN: 礼仪、礼节：房间里谁先谁后
senses.definition: the accepted rules of formal behavior and precedence in diplomacy or ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 外交或仪式中公认的正式行为与位次规则
senses.example: The young attaché was criticized for breaking protocol.
senses.exampleCN: 那位年轻随员因违反礼节而受到批评。
senses.why: French extended the word to 'formula of diplomatic etiquette', attested in English by 1896. The first sheet of a treaty recorded the order of ceremony, so the sheet became the order itself.
senses.whyCN: 法语把这个词扩展为“外交礼仪的程式”，1896 年在英语中出现。条约的首张贴纸记录仪式次序，于是那张纸就变成了次序本身。

senses.title: The prescribed steps: an operating procedure
senses.titleCN: 规程：一步一步照做的那套规矩
senses.definition: an official procedure or set of rules for carrying out a task
senses.definitionCN: 执行某项任务的官方程序或规则
senses.example: Staff must follow the safety protocol when handling chemicals.
senses.exampleCN: 员工处理化学品时必须遵守安全规程。
senses.why: Once protocol means the official record of how something is done, it easily means the prescribed way to do it. The written order of a ceremony becomes the written order of any operation.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 protocol 指“某事如何进行的官方记录”，它就很容易指“规定的进行方式”。仪式的书面次序，变成了任何操作的书面次序。

senses.title: The plan of the experiment
senses.titleCN: 实验方案：写在前面的研究步骤
senses.definition: a detailed written plan for a scientific experiment or clinical trial
senses.definitionCN: 科学实验或临床试验的详细书面计划
senses.example: The trial protocol specifies doses, check-ups and stopping rules.
senses.exampleCN: 试验方案规定了剂量、检查和终止规则。
senses.why: Science keeps the old 'draft, minutes' sense alive: before anything is done, the plan is written down on the first sheet. A protocol is the document that tells the researcher what may be done.
senses.whyCN: 科学保留了古老的“草稿、记录”义：在做任何事之前，计划先被写在首页上。方案就是告诉研究者可以做什么的那份文件。

senses.title: Rules between machines: the computer protocol
senses.titleCN: 计算机协议：机器之间的外交礼节
senses.definition: a set of rules governing how data is exchanged between computers or devices
senses.definitionCN: 规定计算机或设备之间如何交换数据的规则集合
senses.example: HTTP is the protocol your browser uses to fetch a web page.
senses.exampleCN: HTTP 是浏览器抓取网页时使用的协议。
senses.why: Computers need the same thing diplomats need: an agreed order for who speaks first and how a message is acknowledged. The 20c technical sense borrows the word for rules of exchange.
senses.whyCN: 计算机需要的东西与外交官相同：约定谁先发言、消息如何确认的次序。20 世纪的技术义借用了这个表示“交换规则”的词。

senses.title: The first sheet: original draft and minutes
senses.titleCN: 原始记录、草案：贴在卷首的那张纸
senses.definition: the original draft of a document, or the minutes of a transaction (now obsolete)
senses.definitionCN: 文件的原始草稿，或交易的会议记录（现已废弃）
senses.example: The clerk kept the protocol of the negotiations in a leather ledger.
senses.exampleCN: 书记员把谈判的原始记录保存在一本皮面账册里。
senses.why: Greek prōtokollon literally meant 'first sheet glued onto a manuscript', where the contents were listed. English took it in the 1540s as the draft or minutes — the literal sheet before the finished text.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 prōtokollon 字面就是“贴在文稿上的第一张纸”，上面列着目录。英语在 16 世纪 40 年代借入时指草稿或会议记录——成文之前的那张实指纸片。

senses.title: The standard treatment plan
senses.titleCN: 治疗方案：医院里的标准流程
senses.definition: a standard plan for treating a particular illness or condition
senses.definitionCN: 治疗某种疾病或状况的标准方案
senses.example: Patients on the new protocol showed fewer side effects.
senses.exampleCN: 采用新治疗方案的患者副作用更少。
senses.why: Medicine borrowed the research-protocol sense and applied it to care: a fixed sequence of tests and drugs that every patient on the plan receives.
senses.whyCN: 医学借用了研究方案的义项，并把它用到治疗上：一套固定的检查与用药顺序，凡进入该方案的患者都照此接受。

senses.title: The diplomatic instrument
senses.titleCN: 外交文书：正式归档的那份文件
senses.definition: a formal diplomatic document, especially one recording an agreement or understanding
senses.definitionCN: 正式的外交文件，尤指记录某项协议或谅解的文件
senses.example: The protocol was deposited with the foreign ministry.
senses.exampleCN: 这份议定书已交存外交部。
senses.why: In 19c diplomacy, protocol named the document signed by friendly powers to secure certain ends by peaceful means. It is the treaty sense given a formal, archival body.
senses.whyCN: 在 19 世纪外交中，protocol 指友好国家为以和平方式实现某些目标而签署的文件。它是条约义项获得了正式、可归档的形体。

senses.title: Precedence at a state occasion
senses.titleCN: 礼宾次序：国事场合的座次表
senses.definition: the order of precedence and ceremony observed on formal state or institutional occasions
senses.definitionCN: 正式国事或机构场合所遵循的位次与仪式次序
senses.example: Seating followed strict protocol, with the dean at the head of the table.
senses.exampleCN: 座次遵循严格的礼宾次序，院长坐在长桌首位。
senses.why: The etiquette sense widened from diplomacy to any formal hierarchy. Who walks in first, who sits where — the old first sheet still dictates the order of the room.
senses.whyCN: 礼仪义从外交扩展到任何正式等级场合。谁先入场、谁坐哪里——那张古老的首张贴纸仍在规定房间里的次序。

intro.en: Protocol begins as bookbinding: a sheet of contents glued to the front of a manuscript. From that 'first sheet' come the draft, the official record, the treaty, the etiquette of diplomats, the plan of an experiment, and finally the rules that let computers talk.
intro.cn: protocol 起于书籍装订：一张目录纸贴在文稿卷首。从这张“首张贴纸”衍生出草稿、官方记录、条约、外交礼节、实验方案，最后是让计算机彼此交谈的规则。

items.en: Prōtokollon meant 'first sheet glued onto a manuscript', from prōtos 'first' plus kolla 'glue'. The origin of kolla itself is uncertain, so that element is marked source uncertain.
items.cn: prōtokollon 意为“贴在文稿上的第一张纸”，由 prōtos“第一”加 kolla“胶水”构成。kolla 本身的来源不确定，因此这一成分标为“来源不确定”。

items.en: Protocollum meant 'draft', literally 'the first sheet of a volume', on which contents and errata were written. The physical sheet becomes a textual record.
items.cn: protocollum 意为“草稿”，字面是“一卷书的第一张纸”，上面写着目录和勘误。实指的纸片变成了文本记录。

items.en: Prothocole passed into French, where the sense developed from 'rough draft; original copy of a treaty' to 'official record of a transaction' to 'diplomatic document'.
items.cn: prothocole 传入法语，词义从“粗略草稿、条约原件”发展为“交易的官方记录”，再发展为“外交文件”。

items.en: English first records prothogol 'prologue' (mid-15c.), then prothogall 'draft of a document, minutes of a transaction, original of any writing' (1540s). These senses are now obsolete.
items.cn: 英语最早记录 prothogol“序言”（15 世纪中），随后记录 prothogall“文件草稿、交易记录、任何文书的原件”（16 世纪 40 年代）。这些义项今已废弃。

items.en: 'Diplomatic document signed by friendly powers' develops through the 17c.–19c.; the French sense 'formula of diplomatic etiquette' is attested in English by 1896.
items.cn: “友好国家签署的外交文件”一义在 17 至 19 世纪发展起来；法语“外交礼仪程式”这一义项于 1896 年在英语中出现。

items.en: 'Conventional proper conduct' is recorded from 1952. The technical sense 'rules for exchanging data between computers' arose in the 20c. as engineers borrowed the idea of an agreed order of exchange.
items.cn: “约定俗成的得体举止”记录于 1952 年。技术义“计算机之间交换数据的规则”在 20 世纪出现，工程师们借用了“约定的交换次序”这一观念。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the proto- opening but differs in the second element; the meaning group shares the idea of rules or formal agreement, not the shape.
note.cn: 形近组共享 proto- 开头，但第二成分不同；近义组共享“规则或正式约定”的概念，而非外形。

entries.definition: a first model from which later versions are developed. It shares proto- 'first' but ends in -type, not -col.
entries.definitionCN: 原型；最初模型。它共享 proto-“第一”，但词尾是 -type，不是 -col。

entries.definition: a hypothetical first cell. It looks like protocol but its second element is 'cell'.
entries.definitionCN: 原始细胞（假想中的最初细胞）。它形似 protocol，但第二成分是“细胞”。

entries.definition: a positively charged particle in the nucleus. The word means 'the first one', with no 'glue' element.
entries.definitionCN: 质子。这个词意为“第一个”，没有“胶水”这一成分。

entries.definition: the opening of a play or book. It also means 'first speech', but from logos rather than kolla.
entries.definitionCN: 序言；开场白。它也指“最先的话”，但来自 logos 而非 kolla。

entries.definition: an arrangement people accept. It is broader and less formal than a protocol.
entries.definitionCN: 协议；一致意见。它比 protocol 更宽泛、更不正式。

entries.definition: the conventional rules of polite behavior. It matches protocol's ceremonial sense.
entries.definitionCN: 礼节；礼仪。它对应 protocol 的仪式义。

entries.definition: an established way of doing something. It matches protocol as an operating sequence.
entries.definitionCN: 程序；步骤。它对应 protocol 作为操作流程的义项。

entries.definition: a widely accepted custom or practice. It is unwritten where protocol is often written.
entries.definitionCN: 惯例；公约。它常是不成文的，而 protocol 常是成文的。

entries.definition: a formal written agreement between states. It is the legal core of protocol sense 01.
entries.definitionCN: 条约。它是 protocol 第 1 义项的法律核心。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Greek kolla 'glue', prōtokollon 'first sheet', and the modern protocol stack that keeps machines in order.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：希腊语 kolla“胶水”、prōtokollon“首张贴纸”，以及让机器守秩序的现代协议栈。

normal.en: proto- 'first' + kollon 'glue': the first sheet glued to the scroll — protocol.
normal.cn: proto-“第一”+ kollon“胶水”：贴在卷首的第一张纸——protocol。

normal.en: The first sheet listed contents, so protocol came to mean the plan and the record.
normal.cn: 首张贴纸列着目录，所以 protocol 后来既指方案也指记录。

normal.en: Diplomatic protocol is a treaty's first page turned into behaviour.
normal.cn: 外交礼节就是条约的第一页变成了行为举止。

normal.en: A lab protocol is the first sheet of an experiment, written before anyone starts.
normal.cn: 实验室方案就是实验的首张贴纸，在任何人动手之前写好。

normal.en: A network protocol is etiquette for machines: who speaks, in what order, and how to reply.
normal.cn: 网络协议就是机器的礼节：谁先说、按什么次序、如何回应。

abstract.en: One idea runs through all senses: an agreed order written at the front and then obeyed.
abstract.cn: 一个观念贯穿所有义项：写在最前面、随后被遵守的约定次序。

abstract.en: The word moves from paper to people to machines without changing its logic.
abstract.cn: 这个词从纸面走到人，再走到机器，逻辑始终没变。

abstract.en: Protocol is the price of cooperation: someone must go first, and everyone must know it.
abstract.cn: 协议是合作的代价：总得有人先来，而所有人都得知道这一点。

examples.en: The Kyoto Protocol set binding targets for greenhouse gases.
examples.cn: 《京都议定书》为温室气体设定了有约束力的目标。

examples.en: Nurses check the protocol before administering a new drug.
examples.cn: 护士在给新药之前会核对规程。

examples.en: The two networks could not talk because they used different protocols.
examples.cn: 这两个网络因使用不同的协议而无法通信。

dict_mnemonic.text: proto（第一）+ col（胶水）——贴在卷首的第一张纸，写着规矩；谐音“普罗托科尔”：先（pro）把规矩贴在开头，大家照做 → protocol 协议；礼仪

root: 源自希腊语 prōtokollon“贴在文稿卷首的第一张纸”，由 prōtos“第一”加 kolla“胶水”构成，经中世纪拉丁语 protocollum 与古法语进入英语；核心是“写在前头、必须遵守的次序”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses built on one physical thing: the first sheet glued to a document. That sheet held the contents and the order, so protocol became draft, record, treaty, etiquette, procedure, experiment plan, treatment plan, and the rules by which computers exchange data.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都建筑在同一个实物上：贴在文件卷首的第一张纸。那张纸写着目录与次序，于是 protocol 依次成为草稿、记录、条约、礼节、规程、实验方案、治疗方案，以及计算机交换数据的规则。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the first sheet glued to the front of a scroll, listing the order of what follows.
core.cn: 核心意象：贴在卷首的第一张纸，列明后续内容的次序。

branches.en: THE DOCUMENT: the original draft and minutes, and the formal agreement they grow into.
branches.cn: 文书：原始草稿与会议记录，以及由此长成的正式协议。

branches.en: THE ORDER OF PEOPLE: diplomatic etiquette and the precedence observed at state occasions.
branches.cn: 人的次序：外交礼节，以及国事场合遵循的位次。

branches.en: THE WRITTEN PLAN: operating procedures, experiment protocols and standard treatment plans.
branches.cn: 书面方案：操作规程、实验方案与标准治疗方案。

branches.en: THE INSTRUMENT: the formal diplomatic document deposited with a ministry.
branches.cn: 正式文书：交存外交部的正式外交文件。

branches.en: THE RULES OF EXCHANGE: the protocol that lets machines speak to one another.
branches.cn: 交换规则：让机器彼此交谈的协议。

intro.en: Protocol is proto- plus koll- plus -on. Its family shows the Greek prefix prōto- 'first' and the glue-root kolla, which also reaches English through collage and collagen.
intro.cn: protocol 是 proto- 加 koll- 再加 -on。它的词族展示希腊前缀 prōto-“第一”与“胶水”词根 kolla，后者也通过 collage、collagen 进入英语。

latinIntro.en: Greek prōtos 'first' yields the combining form proto-; Greek kolla 'glue' is the base of protocol, collage and collagen, though the deeper origin of kolla is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 prōtos“第一”给出构词成分 proto-；希腊语 kolla“胶水”是 protocol、collage、collagen 的基础，不过 kolla 更深层的来源不确定。

items.meaning: the first sheet glued on; rules and records
items.meaningCN: 协议；礼仪；规程（首张贴纸）
items.example: The hospital follows a strict protocol for infection control.
items.exampleCN: 这家医院遵循严格的感染控制规程。

items.example: The team built a prototype before mass production.
items.exampleCN: 团队在大规模生产之前造了一个原型。

items.meaning: the first actor; the leading character
items.example: The protagonist narrates the whole novel.

items.exampleCN: 原生动物生活在池水中。

items.meaningCN: 质子（核中的“第一个”粒子）
items.example: A proton carries a positive charge.

items.meaning: the original living substance of a cell
items.meaningCN: 原生质（细胞的原初生命物质）
items.example: Early biologists studied the protoplasm of cells.
items.exampleCN: 早期生物学家研究细胞的原生质。

items.meaning: the period just before written history
items.meaningCN: 原史时期（有文字记载之前的那一段）
items.example: Protohistory covers cultures that left no writing.
items.exampleCN: 原史时期涵盖没有留下文字的文化。

items.meaning: a picture made by gluing pieces together
items.meaningCN: 拼贴画（把碎片粘在一起）
items.example: The artist made a collage from old photographs.
items.exampleCN: 这位艺术家用旧照片做了一幅拼贴画。

items.meaning: the protein that 'produces glue' in skin and bone
